articleTitle: Electric Field Strength and Tree Propagation Speed for Electrical Treeing in Silicone Gel
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recently, silicone gel is used to encapsulate electric devices and power modules. Though a silicone gel is insulation, partial discharge is caused by the application of high electric field strength due to the miniaturization of devices, for example. In the gel, the partial discharge trace known as electrical treeing is observed. The generation and propagation of the tree has not become clear. In this research, we investigated the effect of the electric field against development of the treeing, and the influence of the degree of crosslinking of the gel on the tree propagation speed.

articleTitle: The Impact of Impregnating Resins in Ensuring the Reliability of Inverter-Fed Machines
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Impregnating resins are a key component of low voltage motor insulation but are not entirely designed keeping in mind their dielectric properties as they should withstand limited electrical stress. With power electronics, electrical stress can exceed the threshold for partial discharge inception leading to failure in short times. The reliability of the insulation thus becomes more dependent on the performance of the impregnating resins since impregnation raises the partial discharge inception voltage. We have investigated impregnating resins finding that, sometimes, perform in unexpected way at elevated temperatures. Besides, using an infrared camera, we have observed how impulse voltages having elevated slew rates impact on impregnated twisted pairs. The results suggest that bare twisted pairs do not change their temperature appreciably, whereas impregnated twisted pairs can display some increase in the temperature, signaling the presence of large dielectric losses.

articleTitle: Investigation of Partial Discharge Activity in the Slot of a Hairpin-wound Stator
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The reliability of electric vehicles is a key aspect for the entire market. Namely, the lifetime of the electric motor is critical. Therefore, it is necessary to know the stress, ageing factors and the condition of the motor. Higher frequency harmonics, steep slew rates and increasing voltage levels driven by state-of-the-art inverters increase the electric stress imposed on the motor winding insulation, which may lead to partial discharges (PD). If PD occurs, the lifetime of the electrical machine can be reduced to unacceptable levels. Hence, the qualification and lifetime evaluation of inverter-fed machines are of high relevance. It is difficult to identify the exact cause of PD when a complete stator is tested because of its complex structure. In order to investigate PD phenomena in the turns of a hairpin-wound stator, a miniaturized test block representing a single slot of the stator is constructed, in which multiple conductors can be placed. The winding configuration is based on a symmetric three-phase delta connected winding in which, each phase has three parallel paths, i.e., conductors from multiple parallel paths of the same phase are present in each slot in various combinations. The aforementioned test setup is used to investigate the partial discharge inception and extinction voltages (PDIV and PDEV) of various turn-to-turn configurations.

articleTitle: Electrical Insulation at 800 V Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Currently, electric vehicles use drive-fed traction motors that rely on 400 V power supplies. But factors such as motor size, operating temperature, power, efficiency, batteries, and charging time are leading a push toward higher voltages. Accordingly, motor and power electronic designers and producers are targeting 800 V. However, this voltage could be a source of electrical stresses on electrical insulation systems. Because the insulation used in low-voltage motors is too thin, the insulation system risks being subjected to the same electrical field strength as with high-voltage motors. This article describes the potential stresses on insulation systems associated with pulse width modulated drives. Solutions for detecting insulation issues and methods of increasing insulation system function will also be presented.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Power Transformer Failures using the Mixed Weibull Statistics
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A method for evaluating replacement life of substation transformers required to build an asset management system is presented. The electrical utilities are replacing the transformers at the time when the failure rate of the transformers increases to prevent sudden failures. In this study, the mean time to failure of the transformers was defined as the technical end of life, and 52 years was calculated by analyzing the cumulative density function of the failure data. The replacement time of the transformers was defined as the strategic end of life, and 32 years was calculated by failure rate (Bathtub curve) analysis. These lives of the substation transformers are calculated based on 154kV three-phase transformers with sufficient failure data, and the lives of 154kV single-phase transformers applied since 1995 should be recalculated when failure data is sufficiently collected. In addition, the replacement life of the transformers should be strategically decided according to the business value of the company and the risk associated with the failure of the transformer.

articleTitle: Electrical Tree Propagation in Epoxy Resin under Bipolar Square Wave Field with Varied Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Epoxy resin, used as the insulation material of solid state transformer, has to endure the harsh operating conditions of bipolar square wave voltage with high frequency. It is necessary to study the behavior of electrical tree induced by divergent field under bipolar square wave field. In this work, the morphology, growing properties, fractal dimension and breakdown characteristics of electrical tree in epoxy resin under bipolar square wave field with varied frequency was investigated. The voltage frequencies changed from 4 kHz to 20 kHz at 10 kV and 50% duty cycle. The results showed that electrical trees were all branch-like in the experiment. The electrical tree grew rapidly with treeing time after a period with slow propagation and accelerated by higher frequency. Furthermore, the growing speed was increased while number of branches decreased when frequency increased. There existed a maximum fractal dimension when frequency increased from 4 kHz to 20 kHz, which is ascribed to the synergistic effect of polarity reversal and decay of space charge produced by high voltage needle tip and partial discharge. It is suggested that carbon substance was deposited on the channel wall of electrical tree, which was revealed by Raman spectroscopy. The field-driven tree growth (FDTG) model was utilized to explain the development of darker and wider channel originating from ground to needle tip.

articleTitle: Dielectric Breakdown and Partial Discharge Properties of Nanocomposites for Epoxy/Mica Insulation system in Large-size Rotating Machines
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Large-size rotating machine is a key power apparatus for the stability of electric power supply. However, aged machines are increasing and renewals of these machines are desired to avoid the risk of a sudden failure and to keep stable supply of electric power. In the renewal, efficiency improvement and power loss reduction are strongly required from the viewpoint of energy saving and global warming gas reduction. Improvement of insulating material is a promising solution for higher loss efficiency. With this background, we started R & D project with support by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) of Japan, which focused on developments of new insulating materials using nanocomposite technologies and its application to rotating machines. In this paper, concept of the project and some results obtained so far are presented.

articleTitle: Q(t)-measurements of Electrically Deteriorated Polymeric Materials Under Environmental Testing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The charge current integration method (Q(t)-measurement) A Q(t)-meter is an extremely effective method for detecting deterioration or an unusual state in electrical insulation materials. To measure its effectiveness in a severe use case, we conducted Q(t)-measurements using an environmental test. Heat treatment tests at temperatures of 20°C and 60 °C with humidity treatments were conducted on a metal glaze resister and virgin polymeric sample (epoxy resin) while taking Q(t)-measurements. The results show that a high-temperature environment had a significant effect on the level of charge integration, while a high-humidity environment had little effect when not in a condensed atmosphere. However, a polymer sample with a branched electrical tree showed no change from the virgin sample, though it did appear to be easily detectible owing to a change in the obtained voltage. The change of electrical conductivity was caused approximately 50°C, which seems to be related to the glass transition temperature. However, a sort of threshold voltage may not have been changed so that the results of the Q(t)-measurement were not affected by the extension of a kind of electrical tree.

articleTitle: Study on Characteristics of Electrical Tree in Epoxy Resin Measured by Current Integrated Charge Method
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this study, the deterioration of epoxy resin was diagnosed by the current integrated charge method under DC non-uniform electric field. This method is expected as a new diagnostic method for evaluating charge injection and charge generation under a DC high electric field. As a result, several information on the electrical tree was obtained before dielectric breakdown.

articleTitle: Study on Space Charge Behavior in DC Model Cable under Thermal Gradient and Polarity Reversal
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Research on space charge related to HVDC cables is mostly achieved on small scale samples, being flat specimen or reduced size cables, for questions of cost, easiness and flexibility of tests. Resorting to measurements on model cables, there exist different ways of implementing tests using the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) method. In this communication we turn back to the different possible arrangements and show that using a dedicated cable loop for applying the voltage pulse can be a suitable way. Some results are shown in presence of a thermal gradient.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization and 3D Printing: Toward a Functionally Graded Solid Insulator
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Topology optimization and three-dimensional (3D) printing have recently attracted attention as potential technologies for ensuring the application of a functionally graded material to solid insulators of high-voltage power apparatuses. Topology optimization is a mathematical method by which the permittivity or conductivity distribution of a functionally graded solid insulator in a complex insulation system can be optimized. 3D printing can be used to obtain a solid insulator with a controlled permittivity or conductivity distribution. This study introduces research topics on topology optimization and 3D printing to develop a functionally graded solid insulator in Nagoya University.

articleTitle: Influence of High Frequency Voltage with Harmonic Contents and Temperature on Breakdown of Epoxy Resin Used in Power Electronic Transformer
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Insulation in medium-frequency transformers of power electronic equipment usually suffers from the high-frequency voltage stresses, sharp-pulsed voltages and high temperature, leading to the dielectric breakdown failure. Besides, the harmonic contents are included in the high-frequency voltage waveform. It plays an important role in the insulation stress and dielectric loss under high-frequency fields. This paper studies the dielectric breakdown characteristics of the epoxy resin used in medium-frequency transformers under different frequencies voltages and temperatures. Particularly, the effects of harmonic voltages on breakdown strength are considered and discussed. The high-frequency breakdown test platform is used to measure breakdown voltage, including adjustable frequency sinusoidal voltage source (up to 20 kV) and oil bath heating system (up to 200 °C). The frequency of the applied voltage can be reached to 10 kHz. Weibull distribution analysis was employed to discuss the influence of frequency and temperature on dielectric breakdown characteristics of epoxy resin. The experimental results indicated that the breakdown strength of the epoxy resin decreases significantly with the increase of the frequency. Meanwhile, it decreases with an increase in temperature. The breakdown strength under 8 kHz is about 30% lower than 500 Hz at 120 °C. While it (120 °C) is about 15% lower compared to that of 30 °C at 8 kHz. It can be concluded that frequency has a greater effect on breakdown strength compared to temperature. In addition, the electric stresses of the contained harmonic voltages are enhanced under high voltage. Furthermore, the dielectric loss caused by the harmonic voltages presents a large proportion of the total dielectric loss. Hence, the breakdown analysis pointed out that the dielectric heating together with the high electric stresses contributes to the rapid breakdown of the epoxy resin.

articleTitle: The Effect of Geraphene on the Thermal and Dielectric Properties of Epoxy Resin
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Polymer dielectrics are the most popular materials that have been used in energy storage applications. This returns to its high dielectric strength as well as energy storage capabilities. Recently, polymer composites have been developed for this purpose. One of the promising fillers that can be added for this application is graphene particles due to its high energy storage capacity. Thus, this study aims to increase the energy storage capacity of epoxy resin by incorporating different loading of graphene particles. The prepared samples of graphene-epoxy composites were fabricated with 0.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% weight percentages of graphene content. Thermal Gravimetric Analysis (TGA) was used to study the thermal stability of the prepared samples of graphene-epoxy composites. On the other hand, the relative permittivity and the dissipation factor for each prepared sample were evaluated by measuring its resistance and capacitance using LCR meter with equivalent parallel model. The obtained measurements indicated that the thermal stability and the dielectric properties of the selected epoxy resin were successfully improved by incorporating of graphene particles within the polymer chains of the epoxy resin. The best filler loading of graphene-epoxy composites was identified considering the thermal stability and the dielectric properties.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Partial Discharge in XLPE during Electrical Tree Initiation Process under Different Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In order to research the characteristics of partial discharge (PD) during electrical tree initiation process under different temperatures, an AC electrical tree experiment with PD detection and pulse sequence analysis (PSA) was carried out in this paper. The pin-plate electrode was applied to simulate the field concentration areas in cable insulation. Samples of crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) were prepared and the experiment was carried out under 20°C, 60 °C and 90°C. The applied voltage started from 3 kV and increased at a step of 2 kV until the electrical tree was initiated or the voltage reached 15 kV, where each voltage was kept steady for 30 minutes. The results showed that no PD signal was detected and electrical tree was not initiated at 20°C. At 60 °C, the magnitude of PD increased with the increased voltage but the electrical tree was still not initiated. As the temperature increased to 90°C, the magnitude of PD was significantly greater than that at 60°C, and the tree was initiated at 9 kV. The point clusters in the PSA spectrum at 90°C are more scattered than those at 60 °C that is because the initiation of electrical tree causes the change of discharge channel, so PD changes easily at 90°C. Therefore, under the given conditions, the increase in temperature enhances the magnitude of PD and promotes the initiation of electrical tree. When temperature rises, the molecular segments of XLPE move violently, making them disperse, bend, fold, and even fracture. Then space charge accumulates in the polymer and causes local electric field distortion. Local high electric field causes indistinguishable tiny cavities in the polymer, resulting in minute PD but no tree. Moreover, as the temperature further increases, the material would inevitably soften or even deform. The invisible tiny cavities near the needle are thermally expanded, eventually leading to the PD increases and the initiation of electrical tree.

articleTitle: The Application of Signal Processing Using Dual Domain Deconvolution for New Space Charge Measurement Method in HVDC Full-Size Cables
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This article deals with the space charge measurement for full size HVDC cables by means of Pulse Electro Acoustic (PEA) method. We propose improvements in terms of both hardware and signal processing. Electrically insulating material was applied as the acoustic coupler to make it possible to apply the probing pulse voltage onto the measuring point, whilst, the other part of the cable was grounded. For signal calibration we propose a lock-in acquisition to take the reference signal simultaneously with the acquisition of the target signal. This was realized by modulating the poling DC high voltage applied onto the insulation. The deconvolution process is one of the most essential points to determine the charge distribution. Frequency domain deconvolution is often performed in order to normalize frequency spectrum and find the impulse response; however, as low frequency components in both target and reference signals are normally suppressed due to the frequency characteristics of the measurement system, it often leads to a high intensity of unnecessary spurious components. As a solution we propose the dual domain deconvolution. The target signal is once deconvoluted in time domain. This process prevents from the low-frequency spurious but requires longer calculation time compared with the frequency domain processing. Downsampling the signals prior to the process reduces the calculation time; however effective bandwidth may be reduced, leading to the reduction in time (spatial) resolution. It is proposed that combining the low frequency components deconvoluted in time domain after being down-sampled and the high frequency components deconvoluted in frequency domain gives a quick and precise signal processing. The proposed method has practically been applied to the cable measurement.

articleTitle: Effect of Moisture on Space Charge Characteristics of Oil-paper Insulation under AC-DC Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Space charge characteristics of oil-paper insulation with 0.34%-2.72% moisture contents were investigated under AC superposed DC electric field. The phase resolution of space charge detection was 1.79°. Combined with working condition, the superposition ratio of AC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</sub> to DC was set as 1:3. The results show that homocharge accumulates obviously near both electrodes at 3 s polarization, and the density of the homocharge is related to the alternating field, showing a sinusoidal fluctuation. As the moisture content of the sample is within 0.34<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>-2.72<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, the total charge density inside the sample, as well as the conductivity of the sample, increases with the increase of moisture. When moisture content is between 0.34<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to 0.98%, homocharge accumulation of the semi-conductive (SC) electrode is dominant in the bulk of the sample. While moisture content is 2.72%, heterocharge accumulation occurs near both electrodes. This may be due to a lower injection barrier and higher charge mobility after the increase of moisture. Furthermore, the electric field distortion rate increases significantly as the moisture increases, and it even reaches 122% for the 2.72%-moisture content sample, which is triple that of the 0.34<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>-moisture content sample. As the moisture raises, the enhanced space charge accumulation and electric field distortion pose a great threat to the insulating properties of oil-paper insulation and deserve more attention.

articleTitle: Analysis of Discharge Erosion Processes in Epoxy Silica Nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: It is well documented that epoxy/nanofiller composites show superior PD resistant properties to neat epoxy resins, but the compositional changes in surface state during erosion have not been much investigated. This study clarified more detailed behaviors on the compositional change of atomic components precipitated on the surface of epoxy resin specimens after partial discharges (PDs) and glow discharges (GDs) by SEM-EDX method. Further, behaviors of carbon emission from epoxy resin being eroded during glow discharge were clarified by GD-OES method. It is suggested that preferential sputtering might take place in GD sputtering processes.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Inception Voltage Characteristics at Low Frequencies: The Role of Electrostatic Charges
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Standards like the IEC 60502 and IEEE 400.2 support the possibility of utilizing Very Low Frequency supplies in testing of MV and HV cables insulation. Those systems have been employed for several years and have the advantage of requiring relatively small sized equipment. Partial discharge measurement is a common test done to highlight and identify different defects in the insulation system and supposedly obtaining a result reasonably close to the outcome of a test done in operating conditions. The aim of this paper is to investigate the discrepancies introduced by this method, from a theoretical and experimental point of view. In this paper, the case of an internal defect will be analyzed. A simple mathematical model for a real defective insulation, and experimental validation on XLPE and polypropylene, assess the importance on field distribution (hence Partial Discharge activity) of electrostatic buildup on internal surfaces. Depending on the properties of insulating materials, this has a deep effect on the inception voltage at low frequencies, increasing or decreasing PDIV in VLF with respect to the values found at industrial frequencies.

articleTitle: A Round-Robin Test Study of Partial Discharge Inception Voltage in Aeronautic Cables
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Future aircraft systems should consider the partial discharge (PD) phenomena as particularly critical, given the low-pressure environment and the stresses from pulse-width modulated (PWM) voltage at relatively high fundamental frequencies of 1 kHz and above. This work addresses the repeatability of PD Inception and Extinction Voltage (PDIV and PDEV respectively) measurements obtained on different configurations of aeronautic wires following the practical testing procedures described in different existing standards. We show that substantial differences in the results can be obtained according to sample configuration and according to the actual implementation of the standardized test procedures by different laboratories carrying out the experiments.

articleTitle: Thermo-Mechanical Properties of LDPE/SiO2 Nanocomposites based on Chemically Functionalized SiO2 Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Due to its excellency as electrical insulating materials, low density polyethylene, LDPE, must have improved thermal and mechanical properties to tolerate the worst conditions when used in high-voltage insulation systems. One approach is the incorporation of suitable nanoparticles particularly those with a modified surface to meet the chemistry of LDPE matrix. Thus, LDPE/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanocomposites were synthesized using solvent cast method in which different loading of functionalized and un-functionalized SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles were mixed with the molten LDPE in presence of para-xylene as a solvent. The functionalization was performed using vinyl silane as a coupling agent. Thermal gravimetric analysis, TGA, was conducted over the temperature range of 25-600 °C. The same instrument was also used to perform differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) test. For all samples, the temperature that corresponds to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> mass loss were extracted. Beside the TGA, dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) was also performed using Triton Technology dynamic mechanical analyzer in its bending mode. In this test, rectangular samples were heated by 5 °C/min from room temperature to 100 °C at 1.0 Hz frequency. For the selected temperature range, the effects of incorporating SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles, either functionalized or un-functionalized, on storage modulus, loss modulus, and mechanical loss coefficient of LDPE/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanocomposites are investigated.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of surface state of copper conductor of oil-immersed power transformer on sulfur corrosion
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The sulfur corrosion of copper conductors in oil-immersed transformers is affected by the corrosive sulfur content, atmosphere, operating temperature, etc. However, both laboratory studies and field evidences indicate that the influence of the covering state of copper conductors on corrosion should not be ignored. Hence, this paper focuses on the impact of different covering status, including the covering materials and the number of the layers of insulating paper, on the corrosion of copper conductors in thermal aging. The result shows that the existence of a particular gap between the copper conductor and the covering layer is a significant factor to the sulfur corrosion of copper conductors by the concentration cell effect. Insulating paper around copper contributes to a region concentrated with DBDS, Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>and other substances due to the adsorption and impediment effect of insulating paper, which plays a key role in facilitating the sulfur corrosion of copper conductors.

articleTitle: Investigating the Internal Winding Resonance Characteristics of Various Power Transformer Winding Designs
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The transformer is the main equipment in the electricity network, which plays an essential role because the failure of the transformer can cause severe power outages. One of the failures of the transformer is breakdown insulation caused by over-voltage. Failure of the transformer due to over-voltage even still occurs on transformers that are in good condition and also protected by arresters. In this condition, one of the factors suspected as the cause of failure is the phenomenon of resonance over-voltage. Several studies have been conducted to investigate the phenomenon of resonance in the transformer, both the phenomenon of ferro resonance and internal winding resonance. Research conducted is generally related to methods to reduce impacts, both by installing protective equipment and choosing the right design. In this research, the small scale power transformers were designed with different type windings of each phase. Phase A use continuous disc type winding, phase B use shield disc type winding and phase C use closing disc type winding. Measurement points of the tapping locations were located at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% of the full winding. Based on the results of the high frequency characteristics using Sweep Frequency Response Analysis (SFRA), all of the three winding design used in this research shows that there are a tendency of internal winding resonance to occur. Based on that SFRA characteristics, it was found that the highly potential occurrence for internal winding resonance that needs to be considered is the resonance that occur at the frequencies above 100 kHz. According to the SFRA characteristic, frequency above 200 kHz is strongly influenced by series winding capacitance. Hence, based on these results, series capacitance of winding strongly influence the phenomenon of internal winding resonance.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Natural Ester based Insulating Liquid using Hypothesis Testing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: An important element of the power system network is the transformer. The conventional mineral oil (MO), which acts as an insulation and heat transfer agent in a transformer plays a major role in its steadfast operation. The insulation is highly stressed during its operational lifetime. Thus, alternative insulating liquids are being studied to enhance the reliability of the transformer. This paper furnishes a comparative investigation of the breakdown voltages of natural ester-based insulating oil (NEO) and its nanofluids (NEO-NFs) used in power and distribution transformers. The semi-conductive Titanium oxide (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) nanoparticles (NPs) with a suitable weight percentage are dispersed in the base fluid to formulate the NFs. The assessment of the dielectric behaviour of the insulating liquids is studied for all the varieties of oils-NEO, NEO-NF, aged NEO and aged NEO-NF. The oil samples are aged in an open beaker oxidative ageing (OBOA) apparatus. The AC breakdown voltage (ACBDV) is measured using paired spherical electrodes as per the relevant standard. The hypothesis testing is done to ascertain if the breakdown data for all the oil samples follow a particular probability distribution and a statistical analysis is done. The failure probabilities of 5%, 10% and 50% are considered for the distribution functions to analyze the experimental data. It is observed that NEO-NFs performed better than the base fluid in terms of its breakdown value, both before and after ageing process.

articleTitle: Simulation of Space Charge Distribution in the Insulation Layer of XLPE HVDC Cable under Different Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Different temperature distributions may occur in the cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) high voltage direct current (HVDC) cable insulation layer under different laying methods, laying environments, and load currents, which can result in different space charge distributions. In order to investigate the effects of temperature distribution on the space charge behaviors, a pair of ±320 kV XLPE HVDC cables is taken as an example to establish the geometric model. Based on the bipolar charge transport model, the charge distributions in the insulation layer under different load currents are simulated. Results reveal that the accumulated charges are homocharges and distributed near the injection electrode. The amount of charges near the conductor screen is always larger than that near the insulation screen. As the temperature increases, the amount of charges gradually increases, and the distribution range becomes wider. When the temperatures are relatively low, the absolute value of the charge density peak close to the conductor screen monotonically increases with time. However, when the temperatures are relatively high, it shows an non-monotonic fluctuation with time. Besides, the charge accumulations are significantly different when the cables are under different voltage polarities.

articleTitle: The Breakdown Characteristics of Oil-Paper Insulation in Converter Transformers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Oil-paper insulation is the most widely used insulation material in converter transformers, and its safe and reliable operation is one of the important factors to ensure the normal operation of converter transformers. In the long-term working process, the formation and accumulation of space charge in the oil-paper insulation will affect the oil-paper interfacial characteristics and the internal electric field distribution, and will affect the breakdown characteristics. Therefore, it is of practical significance to conduct in-depth study on the charge transport characteristics and breakdown characteristics and mechanism of oil-paper insulation under the influence of space charge. Based on the study of oil-paper insulation breakdown characteristics, this paper systematically studies the space charge characteristics, oilpaper interface characteristics of oil-paper insulation and its breakdown characteristics in different states. Through this research, according to the breakdown strength of oil-paper insulation under different conditions, it can provide support for the design of UHV converter transformers, provide experimental basis for improving the breakdown field strength of oil-paper insulation, and provide a deeper understanding of the solid-liquid interface characteristics based on theoretical study.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Activity of Al2O3 Nanofluid Impregnated Paper Insulation System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Oil-impregnated pressboard (OIP) is preferable insulating medium in power transformers because of its excellent electrical and physical performances. However, under non-uniform fields the degradation of such binary material can be accelerated by partial discharge (PD). In this study Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> oil-based nanofluid is used as a replacement to base oil aiming at improving its PD resistivity. The PD characteristics for both nanofluid impregnated paper (NIP) and OIP were investigated. First, the investigated samples were prepared using a commercially obtained pressboard with a thickness of 1mm. The nanofluid sample was prepared using both stirring and ultrasonic processing. Then, the dried pressboard pieces were impregnated into the nanofluid and base oil inside the vacuum oven. Second, the PD measuring system was manufactured using a needle-plane electrode with a gap spacing of 1 mm. The PD inception voltages (PDIVs) were measured for each sample and were analyzed using Weibull distribution. Then, the PD propagation was estimated at different levels of applied voltage higher than the calculated average inception. The estimation was based on calculating the number of PD pulses for both negative and positive polarity of applied AC voltage. In addition, the time transition of PD pluses for 10 min time domain was depicted for both NIP and OIP. Moreover, the current magnitude of PD pulses and their phase appearance were analyzed. It was found that PD pulses appear around the peaks of the applied AC voltage for both NIP and OIP with a corresponding higher number of pulses for OIP. Based on the obtained results, the role of nanoparticles in PD activity is discussed.

articleTitle: Aircraft Insulation Design for the More Electrical Aircraft: Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper considers the design options to achieve the reliability of random-wound motors fed by silicon carbide inverters and used for the More Electrical Aircraft (MEA). Considering the inception of Partial Discharges as the most severe degradation process, the Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (PDIV) of non-impregnated and impregnated twisted pairs was measured feeding the twisted pairs with a silicone carbide inverter in a partial vacuum. The results show that the margins to ensure that partial discharges are not incepted during operation are tight and that switching to multilevel inverters and hairpin geometries might be necessary if the DC bus voltages will be raised above the current levels (±270 V).

articleTitle: Observation and Modeling of Water Tree in 60 kV-class XLPE Cable-Investigation of AC Loss Current and Electric Field Using Transient Electric Field Analytical Model-
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Water tree is one of the causes of insulation deterioration of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables. In 60 kV-class XLPE cables, elongated water trees may be found as a factor that deteriorates their insulation performance, and it is necessary to detect deterioration signals caused by such water trees in deterioration diagnosis to understand deterioration states of the cables. In this study, we used an electric field analysis software to model an elongated water tree and a bowtie tree observed in 60 kV-class removed aged XLPE cables, and examined influence of the length of the water tree and the position of the bow-tie tree on the AC loss current and the maximum electric field by using transient electric field analysis.

articleTitle: Insulation Design of the UHVDC Submarine Cable under the Background of Global Energy Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The transport capacity, cross-sea distance, and economy of the current extra-high voltage (EHV) DC submarine cables can no longer meet the needs of the global energy interconnection construction, so it is necessary to develop the ultra-high voltage (UHV) DC submarine cable technology. This article first analyzes the specific requirements for UHVDC submarine cables on cross-sea distance, transport capacity, and laying depth. And then, the research and development targets of the insulation of ±800 and ±1100 kV UHVDC submarine cables are investigated combined with the key influencing factors by the electro-thermal coupled finite element simulation.

articleTitle: A Method to Calculate Uncertainty due to Unavailable Data in Transformer Assessment Index
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Transformer Assessment Index (TAI) is a useful tool to rank the power transformers fleet to underline the critical transformers based on multi-parameters. In many cases, the data available for TAI determination is incomplete. Unavailability of the data is one of the limitations of TAI, which it may disguise a poor condition of a transformer as a result of limited data calculation. This paper proposes the use of parameter prioritization results to calculate Certainty Level (CL) due to data availability of a TAI. The proposed approach has been applied to illustrate CL calculation of five scenarios of power transformer data availability. Further illustration has been done to a 150 kV power transformer with six points of measurement data. By expressing the proposed level of uncertainty in addition to the TAI value, the asset manager can obtain better justification in determining the appropriate action for the power transformer operation and maintenance.

articleTitle: Research on Ultraviolet Aging Properties of Modified Silicone Rubber for Composite Insulator
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this paper, the formulation of silicone rubber for composite insulator was performed, and the properties of silicone rubber before and after improvement were analyzed. Furthermore, the ultraviolet aging test was carried out on modified silicone rubber, and the changes of mechanical properties, electrical properties and hydrophobicity with ultraviolet aging time were studied. The results show that the overall performance of the modified silicone rubber is improved significantly, including 44.6% increase in elongation at break, 42.9% increase in volume resistivity, 45.5% increase in breakdown strength and 78.6% decrease in dielectric loss factor. With the increasing of ultraviolet aging from 0h to 5000h, the hardness of modified silicone rubber increase, the tensile strength and elongation at break decrease, in which the elongation at break decrease significantly (by 53.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). The static contact angle has little variation and shows a fluctuating trend, furthermore, the hydrophobicity classes changes from HC1 to HC2. The variation of AC breakdown strength and power frequency dielectric constant of modified silicone rubber are not obvious, but the volume resistivity decrease by 70.2% and the dielectric loss factor increase by 367.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>.

articleTitle: Comparison of Partial Discharge Activity in Mineral Oil and PFAE Containing Multiple Spherical Metal Particles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) induced by the presence of free multiple spherical metal particles in two commercial transformer oils has been measured at ambient temperature and at 40°C in order to develop an effective monitoring system for high voltage transformer. The PD measurement result of a conventional mineral oil has been compared with vegetable-based transformer oil of Palm Fatty Acid Ester (PFAE) under AC applied voltage in quasi-uniform field at three consecutive gaps of 5mm until 9mm. Three different electric field of 1.5kV/mm, 2kV/mm and 2.5kV/mm has been applied at each gap in the PD measurement. The partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) was measured to be 6.7kV and 8kV for PFAE and mineral oil at 9mm gap respectively. The Phase-Resolved Partial Discharge (PRPD) of PFAE and mineral oil at 1.5kV/mm until 2.5kV/mm appeared to have a distinctive characteristic at these different temperatures.

articleTitle: Improved Interface Charge Transport Model of HVDC Cable Joint-Considering Carrier Dynamic Equilibrium
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The Maxwell-Wagner model and the bipolar charge transport model both aim on describing the charge transport behaviours in dielectrics. The Maxwell-Wagner model performs well in calculating the polarization current and the electric field distribution, but it is too macroscopic to describe the microscopic behaviours of space charges. The bipolar charge transport model can well simulate the space charge accumulation, but it cannot quantitatively relate the microscopic transport behaviours with the macroscopic conductivities of dielectrics. Considering the shortages of the above two models, an improved charge transport model, named carrier dynamic equilibrium model, is proposed in this paper by introducing a source term of carrier dynamic equilibrium. And the interface charge accumulation process of the low density polyethylene (LDPE)/ ethylene propylene diene monomer (EPDM) bi-layer dielectric, a typical insulation structure of the cable joint, is simulated by different models. Compared with the Maxwell-Wagner model and the bipolar charge transport model, the improved model has the best coincidence with measurements, which may provide accurate references for the design of HVDC cable joints.

articleTitle: Study of Asymmetrical Leakage Currents of Metal Oxide Surge Arrester due to Multiple Current Impulses
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper presents the study of asymmetrical leakage current of metal oxide surge arrester (SA) after being tested with multiple current impulses. The study is made using 2 SAs specimens of 21 kV rated voltage, 5 kA nominal discharge current. The experiment is divided into 4 steps; 10 shots of positive discharge current impulses, reference voltage measurement, 5 shots of negative discharge current impulses and reference voltage measurement. Initial conditions of the SAs are assessed prior to the testing: temperature measurement, 1 mA reference voltage and resistive leakage current at rated voltage. Then, both specimens are applied current lightning impulses at 200% of rated discharge current (10 kA) and the temperature is measured after. The lightning current impulse is 8/20 μs waveform and the duration between each impulse is 10s. Prior to the application of multiple current impulses, the difference of resistive current peak amplitude of specimen 1 and 2 were 3% and 0.95% respectively. Following positive current lightning impulses, the value changed to be 71.245% and 72.75% respectively. The specimens were then left to cool down in the room temperature for 1 day. After application of negative current lighting impulses, difference of resistive leakage current of specimen 2 changed to be 1.99%, and specimen 1 broke down after 2 impulses. Asymmetrical leakage current phenomena caused by the impulse current may negatively affect the breakdown characteristic of the SA which should be relevant with the collected charge inside the SA material, however, the opposite polarity of the applied impulse currents may eliminate such problem.

articleTitle: Strawberry Like Micro@nano Hybrid Filler for Thermally Conductive Epoxy Composites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Thermally conductive dielectrics are highly desirable for improving the thermal management capability of power equipment. Traditional dielectrics with high thermal conductivity were prepared by filling spherical micro-sized α-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>or mixture of micro- and nano-sized α-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> into an insulating polymer. However, for a long time, this method suffers from low thermal conductivity enhancement. In this method, a new hybrid filler (μm@nm-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) with strawberry-shape encapsulation structure was reported for thermal conductivity enhancement of insulating polymers. The new hybrid filler was prepared by two steps: the micro- and nano-sized α-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> fillers were firstly surface-modified by amino-terminated and epoxide-terminated silane coupling agents, and then the encapsulation process was carried out by chemical bond after reaction. At a filler loading of 65 vol% and the volume ratio of nm-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> to μm-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> of 1:4, the thermal conductivity of the epoxy composites with μm@nm-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> exhibit the optimum of 1.9 W/(m·K), and the achieved thermal conductivity enhancement are 12.1%, 16.2% and 21.5% higher when compared with the composites with physical nm-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> /μm-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> mixture, pure μm-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and pure nm-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, respectively.

articleTitle: Measurement and Evaluation Techniques of Nanocomposites and Functionally Graded Materials for Advanced Electric Power Apparatus
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this project, various evaluations including electrical insulation tests on insulating materials are carried out at each development stage for materials and equipment that are approaching the product level. This paper will provide an overview of these efforts. During the material development stage, there are many instances of trial and error for the composition and other aspects, so evaluation techniques using many small electrode systems are often adopted for the evaluation of the insulation performance. Furthermore, efficient evaluation that uses a small number of samples for the same conditions is required, since there is also trial and error for shape, manufacturing methods, etc. even in the development stages for insulators of sizes and shapes close to those of the actual equipment. Therefore, the impulse charging test using the one-shot method is being examined. In addition, a technique to quantify the dispersion of filler using image processing based on SEM images is currently under development as a common evaluation technique for insulating materials for various types of equipment. Research institutes including universities are conducting studies on the basic physical property evaluation in order to elucidate the function expression mechanisms in newly developed insulating materials.

articleTitle: Effect of Local Arc Discharge on Hydrophobicity Decrease of Silicone Rubber Surface: -Investigation on Hydrophobicity Change by Measuring Water Drop Velocity and Surface Analysis-
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Various methods have been proposed to evaluate hydrophobicity of silicone rubber used for sheds of polymeric insulators. CIGRE WG D1.14 has proposed Dynamic Drop Test (DDT) method to evaluate the hydrophobicity changes of the materials. In this paper, we measured static contact angle, hydrophobicity class in spray method, and drop velocity of water droplets, in order to observe the change in hydrophobicity of silicone rubber surface suffered to local arc discharge at DDT. Because of the hydrophobicity decreases due to the local arc discharge, the water droplet changes from a spherical to a water film. In particular, changes of initial state in hydrophobicity can be observed by measuring the drop velocity of water droplets. And the correlation was confirmed with the cumulative charge of local arc discharge. Therefore, the water drop velocity was effective for the evaluation of hydrophobicity change.

articleTitle: Conduction Phenomena of AC- and DC-XLPE Analyzed by Q(t) Method
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Relaxation time τ (=ε/k) is one of the important dielectric properties, and the τ can be obtained by Q(t) method with an relatively simple treatment. The procedure of the consideration to obtain τ, and measurement results of AC- and DC-XLPE are shown in this article. To consider τ efficiently and effectively, a parameter “charge ratio” was introduced. The charge ratio means a ratio of Q(t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>) which is a charge amount Q(t) at a certain measurement time tm and Q(0) which is an initial rise of voltage application, that is Q(tm)/Q(0). The obtained τ is 300 s for AC-XLPE and more than 28800 s (8 h) for DC-XLPE at 60°C under 60 kV/mm.

Author Keywords: Direct current integrated charge method (Q(t) method)

articleTitle: Effect of Interphase on the Space Charge Performance of Al-Epoxy Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Controlled addition of spherical metallic nanofillers below the percolation threshold has shown improved interfacial properties in mitigating the space charge accumulation over the base epoxy polymer material. The theoretical model is utilized in the present study to elucidate the variation in an interfacial area with the addition of aluminium nanoparticles. It results in the inclusion of nanofiller until a particular filler concentration has shown an increase in the interfacial volume. In contrast, reduction in inter particle distance with the further addition of nanoparticles has shown the reduced interfacial volume. Since the space charge information in a given material is unique at a given instant of time within the bulk, a classification technique, i.e. principal component analysis is employed in classifying the nanocomposite materials having different filler concentrations.

articleTitle: Investigation of Effects of Length and Width of Water Tree in 6.6 kV XLPE Cable on DC Leakage and AC Superposition Currents by Using Transient Electric Field Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A penetrated water tree found in dry-cured and extruded three-layer (E-E type) 6.6 kV cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables was modeled, DC leakage and AC superposition currents were calculated by using transient electric field analysis, and the calculated and measured currents were compared. In addition, water trees were assumed as spheroidal ones, and DC leakage and AC superposition currents were analyzed when the length and width of the water tree changed.

articleTitle: Parallel Measurements of Space Charge Distribution and Q (t)
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Space charge distribution p(x,t) and current integrated charge Q(t) at high electric field (up to 130 kV/mm) in a 250 μm thick low density polyethylene (LDPE) film are measured from 30 to 85 °C by using a assembled device. The electric field and temperature dependences of the resistance component R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and the capacitance component C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> of the sample are calculated and the relation of measured space charge distribution is discussed.

articleTitle: Approach to Asset Management of Substation Equipment in Japan
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: IEC white paper “Strategic Asset management of Power Networks” was published in 2015, and TC123 “Management of network assets in power system” is working towards the IEC standardization since 2017. The environment surrounding Japanese utilities is changing, and the need for asset management is increasing. This paper describes the environment surrounding the electric power industry in Japan and the necessity of asset management. And this paper reports example of asset management for substation equipment (Transformers and circuit breakers) by Japanese utilities. First, the environment surrounding the electric power industry in Japan is summarized. The aging of equipment owned by utilities, the decrease in the number of electric power engineers due to the declining birthrate, and a decrease in demand for electric power are some of the problems facing us. Under these circumstances, it is not realistic to replace equipment based on aging due to cost, construction, and network operational constraints. Because many equipment need to be replaced in a short period. Therefore, in order to realize effective investment and equalization of the replacement amount, asset management based on the condition evaluation and evaluation of consequence is important. Next, this paper reports the case of asset management for substation equipment by some Japanese utilities. This paper describes asset management (such as “scoring”, “risk matrix” and other methods) for transformers and circuit breakers, in which condition evaluation of equipment (such as dissolved gas analysis results of transformers and the number of operations of circuit breakers) and evaluation of consequence (such as power system importance and environmental impacts) are evaluated. In addition, important evaluation items in each case are described.

articleTitle: Surface discharges and flashover voltages: investigation of XLPE samples with SiO2 and Al2O3 nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Since 1994 there is a lot of research effort put into the investigation of nanocomposites and their applications in various fields of high voltage engineering. Among the possible most interesting applications is the field of underground cable insulation. Given the fact that XLPE was proven to be a reliable insulating material in the past decades, modern efforts concentrate into the possible applications of the said material enriched with small wt% of nanoparticles. The samples used were polymer nanocomposite insulating materials. The polymeric material was XLPE, while SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>0<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> were used as nanoparticles. The samples were XLPE with 0 wt% nanoparticles and XLPE with 0.2 wt%, 0.5 wt% and 1 wt% of Si0<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles. Furthermore XLPE with 0.2 wt%, 0.5 wt% and 1 wt% of Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanoparticles were investigated, as well. In the context of the present work, surface discharges as well as flashover voltages were investigated with a variety of XLPE nanocomposites, namely XLPE with various wt% of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanoparticles. A uniform electrode arrangement was used for the experiments, in which AC voltage was applied. Since surface discharges and flashover voltages are strongly influenced by humidity, various water droplet arrangements of different conductivities were positioned on the sample surface. The influence of water droplet positioning, droplet conductivity and number of droplets is investigated. It seems that the above parameters play a decisive role on surface discharges and flashover voltages and that the samples of XLPE with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles give the most encouraging results regarding the flashover voltage.

articleTitle: On the Temporal Variation of Boundary Fields and Non-uniform Distribution of Homocharges in LDPE
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The prime source of accumulated space charges is considered to be the electrode injected charges. Although the injection phenomenon is majorly modeled using the well-known Schottky Injection mechanism, which gives a theoretically constant boundary electric field throughout the duration of the applied field. However, on careful observation of experimental results, obtained from the pulsed electro-acoustic method, a systematic trend of temporal variation can be observed in the boundary electric fields and hence boundary charges. Also, an uneven distribution of homocharges has been observed upon field application throughout the duration of field application, having a larger concentration of holes near anode in comparison to the cathode. Here, the temporal variation of the boundary electric field and corresponding boundary charge has been discussed. Besides this, the reason of uneven distribution of holes is explained with the help of holes transportation using the hopping mechanism.

articleTitle: Effect of Impurity Bridges on Breakdown Strength of PFAE under Lightning Impulse Stress
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This research investigates the effect of cellulose bridging formation on the breakdown strength of Palm Fatty Acid Easter (PFAE) under Standard Lightning Impulse Voltage (SLIV). An impulse generator up to 140kV (max) was used as a source of SLIV and it is applied according to the IEC60897 standard for the breakdown voltage test. The cylindrical test cell with sphere-sphere electrodes gap was utilized in this experiment. The application of DC source to the test cell generates quasi-uniform field between the electrodes gap which form cellulose bridging. The breakdown strength of PFAE was analyzed using a Weibull Cumulative Breakdown Probability. The statically analysis was always compared with the Clean Oil as a reference. Based on the experimental results, the cellulosic particle reduced nearly 4.5% breakdown strength of contaminated PFAE oil. The particle influence on electrical field strength also becomes more prominent and further breakdown more than 24.5% when the bridging is formed. As a conclusion, the present of particles and its bridge structures were headed to the detrimental effect of liquids strength by reduced the field strength of PFAE up to 29% under the lightning impulse stress.

articleTitle: Effect of Pre-heating on AC Breakdown Strength of Oil Barrier Tube
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The dependence on cable technology especially in urban areas is growing rapidly for power transmission and distribution. Various dielectric materials laid foundation for recent advancements in the field of power cables. The medium voltage distribution network with underground power cables consists of different links and joints. This paper discusses the insulation properties of PILC and XLPE cable joint known as transition joint. Prefabricated insulating material like oil barrier tube is been used for better insulating properties and preventing oil leakage from a transition joint. This barrier tube has resulted in initiation of various cable joint damages through electric breakdown. AC breakdown analysis was performed on the oil barrier tube material while interesting results have been achieved due to pre-heating of the samples. Further investigation of the material through SEM-EDS, FTIR, XRD and DSC paved way for better analysis of the material properties through its chemical composition.

articleTitle: Evaluation on Depth Profile of Surface Degradation of Polymeric Insulators by Microscopic Observation of the Cross Section
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Development of evaluation methods and clarification of the degradation mechanisms of silicone rubbers used for the housing material is important to increase the long-term reliability of polymeric insulators. In this research, we investigated the depth profile of surface degradation of polymeric insulators used at an actual 66 kV transmission line for more 10 years. Changes in the ratio of elemental compositions and chemical structures of silicone rubbers were evaluated by microscopic observations of the cross sections using Scanning Electron Microscopy - Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) and Infrared (IR) imaging analysis. As the results, increase of the ratio of Al/Si compositions of the silicone rubbers within approximate 100 μm deep from the surface was observed by SEM-EDX. Also, some changes in the chemical structures, supposedly oxidation of the silicone materials in the same area were defined by IR imaging analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Partial Discharge Detection Technique under Square Wave
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The detection methods of partial discharge (PD) in power equipment insulation under square wave need to consider the displacement current and electromagnetic interference caused by the fast rising and falling edges of the power source. Therefore, there are some differences in PD measurements from those under power frequency sinusoidal wave. In this paper, a PD detection method based on super high frequency (SHF) signal and down-mixing principle is proposed, which suppresses interference through increasing the frequency band of the collected signal and shift the spectrum to lower frequency through down-mixing method to lower the requirements of the acquisition equipment. PD experiments are performed on epoxy specimen with needle-plate defect under the square wave and the SHF mixing method was compared with the pulsed current method and the ultra-high frequency (UHF) method. It is determined that, pulsed current method and UHF method were no longer applicable under the square wave with fast rising edge, while there are some advantages of SHF mixing method in anti-interference and feasibility. Especially for those PDs in solid materials with high insulation strength, it shows high sensitivity and good signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Surface Voltage Measurement of XLPE Insulated Covered Overhead Conductor
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recently, in medium voltage distribution systems, overhead conductors are replaced by insulation covered conductors owing to their profound advantages. The insulated overhead conductor shares a boundary between the dielectric insulation used and the air insulation. Because of the higher insulation resistance of the air when compared with any polymeric insulation, most of the voltage drop will be on the dielectric-air interface (i.e. on the surface of the dielectric). The main goal of this work is to investigate the surface potential of the XLPE covered conductor accurately at different positions using a lab designed voltage divider under applied alternating voltages. Furthermore, 2D simulations have been done to estimate the surface potential of an insulation covered conductor. Interesting results on the surface voltage with applied voltages and different positions in the insulation are presented.

articleTitle: Space Charge and Conduction Current under DC High Stress in Modified Polypropylene
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: XLPE (Cross-linked polyethylene) has been used as an insulating material of solid insulation cables for long years, because of its excellent insulation performance under AC high voltage and advantage on practical use without maintenance. However, a concern that a dielectric breakdown occurs especially under a high DC electric field at a high temperature comes up due to an increase in electric field caused by space charge accumulation. To solve the problem, a modification of XLPE and usages of non-cross-linked materials such as modified polypropylene are studied worldwide recently. We have been studying possibilities of modified polypropylene as new cable insulating materials, and we have evaluated insulation performances of some polypropylene based copolymers by measuring space charge distributions and external circuit currents at high temperature under high DC electric field. In this research, a block and a random copolymerized polypropylene with polyethylene, which show good flexibilities compared to isotactic polypropylene, are investigated. It is found while a space charge injection and its accumulation was observed in the materials as they are, the accumulation characteristics were improved by introducing a polar group to both of the block and the random copolymers under an applied dc electric field of less than 100 kV/mm even at a temperature of 80 °C.

articleTitle: Effect of Background Noise Discrimination on Partial Discharge Pattern Recognition using Neural Network and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this study, the effect of background noise and phase lag phenomena on partial discharge pattern recognition of power cable system was analyzed. For the purpose, recognition rates were compared using SVM and Neural Network through statistical character extraction of the PRPD patterns for the partial discharge data of artificially modelled defects. Using this method, pattern recognition was performed based on the background noise elimination levels and the phase lag modelling. As a result, it was found that too much elimination of background noise would lead to the loss of partial discharge data, resulting in lower recognition rates. And SVM were more vulnerable than Neural Network for the phase lag phenomena.

articleTitle: A Study on Space Charge Behavior in Double-layer Dielectrics for Eco-friendly Power Cable Joint
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recently, Researches on eco-friendly polymer insulating materials that can replace XLPE in HVDC transmission has been actively performed. However, joint boxes are also essential for long distance transmission of eco-friendly HVDC power cables. Therefore, two or more insulating materials exist inside the joint box, and interfaces are formed between the insulating materials. These interfaces are weak point in insulation performance. Especially under dc voltage stressing conditions, dielectric interfaces are a favorite location for charge build-up. In fact, according to the Maxwell-Wagner theory for interfacial polarization, charge accumulates at interfaces if the ratio of the conductivities and that of the permittivity of the two media in contact are not the same. In addition, because of the characteristic properties of the interface a more complex build-up of interfacial charge may occur. In this study, the space charge was measured in the double-layer model in joint box using polymer insulating materials for eco-friendly power cables. In addition, we compared and analyzed the space charge measured in the interface between the XLPE and LSR.

articleTitle: Analysis of Pulsed-electroacoustic Signal Propagation Based on Viscoelastic Model
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Acoustic attenuation of a pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) signal propagating through a polyethylene film is analytically studied using the Kelvin-Voigt model for a viscoelastic material. The transfer functions of low- and high-density polyethylene films in the PEA system are obtained based on the viscoelastic theory, which allow us to directly calculate acoustic attenuations in the polyethylene films. In experiment, low- and high-density polyethylene films with different thicknesses are used as PEA samples to verify the proposed method. The calculated acoustic waveforms show a good agreement with the measurements.

articleTitle: Effect of Catalyst on Dielectric Breakdown Characteristics of Esterified Rice Oil
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Our laboratory has been investigated the dielectric breakdown characteristics of rapeseed and soybean oil. In this study, we studied the effects of catalyst amount and types on kinematic viscosity and AC breakdown characteristics of esterified rice oil. These results were showed as the following. (1) The kinematic viscosity of esterified oil was below 10 [mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/s], which was lower than that of rice oil before the ester exchange reaction. (2) The AC breakdown strength (Fb) of esterified rice oil depended on the type of catalyst. (3) Fb did not change with varying the catalyst (NaOH) amount.

articleTitle: Thermal and Electrical Properties of EP/AlN Nanocomposites at Different Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The epoxy resin (EP) nanocomposites have shown the enhanced thermal and electrical properties for the power electronic packaging application. EP nanocomposite with 1 wt% content of nano-AlN (Aluminum Nitride) filler is prepared in the present study. The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirms the well-dispersed AlN nanofillers inside the EP matrix. The thermal properties are investigated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The DC electrical properties are investigated by the space charge measurements at 30, 50 and 70 °C. Moreover, the average space charge density is calculated from the polarization data of the test samples. The results show that the addition of the nano-AlN can enhance the glass transition temperature of the EP sample. It indicates that the addition of the nano-AlN can improve the thermal stability of EP/AlN nanocomposite. The homo charges accumulate inside the pure EP sample. The addition of the nano-AlN can suppress the space charge accumulation. The space charge accumulation becomes more obvious at high temperature for the pure EP sample. However, the space charge accumulation of the EP/AlN nanocomposite sample is not significant even at 70 °C. Moreover, the accumulated average charge density of the EP/AlN nanocomposite is evidently lesser than pure EP sample. The electric field distortion for the pure EP sample is obviously serious than that of the EP/AlN nanocomposite. Limited space charge accumulation and electric field distortion are found for the EP/AlN nanocomposite sample at 70 °C. Overall, the EP/AlN nanocomposite sample exhibits superior electrical properties at 70 °C.

articleTitle: A New Method of Measuring Electron-hole pairs with The PEA method Just after Electron Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the new measurement method for measuring electron-hole pairs which were generated by electron beam irradiation. High voltage was applied through the vacuum gap to prevent injecting charges from the electrode. In addition, the compering the amount of electron-hole pair by the irradiation current density. As a result, electron-hole pairs were observed in this system, and the amount didn't change by the current density.

articleTitle: Influence of Internal Structure on Dielectric Breakdown Characteristics of Additive Manufacturing Parts Formed by Selective Laser Sintering
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) can be used to easily design and create parts with complex shapes, and hence, it is used in various fields. Recently, AM parts have been developed as not only prototypes but also practical components. Therefore, it is very important to understand the characteristics of these parts. For example, it is important to understand the insulation characteristics of AM-based insulation components. However, these insulation characteristics have not been sufficiently investigated. In this study, we examined the dielectric breakdown characteristics of AM samples manufactured by selective laser sintering (SLS) while considering the effects of the part build orientation of the samples. In addition, we observed the cross section of the samples after dielectric breakdown and studied the void condition and dielectric breakdown path. The void distribution state was also investigated by determining the apparent relative permittivity.
