From the above experiments, the points to note when applying AM components manufactured by SLS to insulating components became clear.

articleTitle: Effect of Thermal Aging on Dielectric Properties of XLPE Insulated HVDC Cable
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Space charge characteristics, leakage current, and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) of the cable insulation were investigated to quantitatively evaluate the thermal aging effects on the dielectric properties of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulated high-voltage direct current (HVDC) cable. The longest aging time of these cables at 135°C and 17kV/mm DC electric field reaches 1440h. The space charge distribution was obtained under multiple electric fields from 5 kV/mm to 35 kV/mm by a full-scale space charge measurement system for cable sample. It is shown that the amount of space charge and decreases after 720h aging, and then decreases after another 720h aging. At the same time, the leakage current increases with the aging time, while the molecular weight and crystallinity of the insulating material decreases with aging time. Based on the results mentioned above, the effect of thermal stress on XLPE DC cable insulation is similar to that on alternating current (AC) cable insulation. Space charge mainly comes from the dissociation of cross-linking by-products and small molecules generated by aging. In the initial stage of aging before 720h, the degassing process dominates, resulting in a decrease in space charge. Between 720h and 1440h of the aging process, the molecular chain breaks into small molecules, and the amorphous area expands, which increases the space charge. Simultaneously, the decrease in crystallinity and the increase in small molecules increase the trap concentration, which reduces space charge mobility leakage current. Reduced charge mobility leads to a decrease in the leakage current.

articleTitle: Application of Cable Diagnosis in the Steel Industry
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The IRC method was applied to evaluate water-tree degradation, a significant cause of failure of power cables in Japan. In addition, an RF diagnosis system that enables online power system diagnosis at a steel plant was tested, and a case study was presented that actually prevented a fault. A combination of these maintenance methods is proposed.

articleTitle: Improved Method for Evaluation of Dielectric Breakdown Strength of Epoxy / Silica Nanocomposite Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Epoxy / silica nanocomposite materials are attracting attention as a promising insulating material for next-generation electric rotating machines. It is empirically known the dielectric breakdown strength of an organic insulating material can be improved by mixing with nano-scale inorganic fillers. However, the role of the inorganic filler in the suppression of the dielectric breakdown is not fully understood yet. In this study, we are developing an efficient method for characterizing dielectric breakdown strength of epoxy / silica nanocomposite material, where the epoxy resin sample is thinned to submicrometer scale to induce the breakdown even at a low voltage and in a short time. The problem with using thin epoxy resin is its fragility; the thin epoxy resin is easily damaged by sticking an electrical probe on it. This problem is resolved by depositing a buffer metal layer on the epoxy resin and employing a metal bead as the electrical probe. It is confirmed by SEM observation that the damage at evaluated point on the epoxy resin is successfully suppressed. Using the bead probe, we successfully monitored the current transition of the dielectric breakdown events.

articleTitle: Effect of Oxygen Vacancy on the Electronic Structure and Electrical Properties of HfO2/Si Interface
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is one of the alternative candidate gate materials for SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in electronic devices, because of its high dielectric constant (ε ≈ 25). Space charges and defects are more favorable to be accumulated at the oxide-substrate interface, which plays a key role in the electrical properties of electronic devices. However, it is still unclear that how the defects affect the electrical performance of devices. In this paper, the effect of oxygen vacancy (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>) on the electronic structure of the HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si interface and electrical properties of devices was analyzed by using the density functional theory. The 2-layer model of HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si was built, and then the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> was introduced into the interface through first-principles calculation method. The interfacial electronic levels, states, and localization functions of these two models were calculated with the assistance of Quantum Espresso software. It was found that the interaction between atoms such as Si-O and Hf-O at HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si interface is weaker than that in the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, respectively. It means that the point defects are easy to be formed at the HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si interface. The interfacial state is originated from Si and Hf atoms, which is quite different from the bulk state and responsible to the electrical performance of devices. Compare with Hf, the Si near V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</inf> processes greater electron affinity and thus has more ability to capture electrons, leading to the electrostatic breakdown eventually. Our research work revealed the reason why the interfacial states were formed and the physical mechanism of the effect of interfacial states on the electrical properties of the device from the electronic level. It is expected that these results can be benefited to the structural design and performance optimization for electronic devices.

articleTitle: Conductivity Distribution in Air by Charging Process on Solid Dielectrics under DC Voltage
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The enhancement of DC electrical insulation performance is required for the reliable HVDC power equipment and bulk power transmission in recent years. In this paper, we measure the charging process on PMMA in air under DC steady-state and investigate the space distribution of the conductivity in air by using needle-air-PMMA-plane electrode configuration. In order to simulate the space distribution of the conductivity in air under DC steady-state, the charge transport equations in air considering the generation, recombination and motion of positive and negative ions are solved. We calculate the space distribution of the conductivity in air activated by partial discharge. As a result, it is quantitatively estimated that highly conductive area in air with approximately 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> times higher conductivity than the other area is formed along the electric line of force from the needle electrode tip as the source of charge carrier.

articleTitle: Study on the relation between PD characteristics and degradation of PP films for power capacitors by utilizing artificially formed through holes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The authors have been investigating the deterioration characteristics of polypropylene (PP) films due to partial discharge (PD) in a closed void as a basic study of long-term deterioration of power capacitors. We reported that (1) the number of PD pulses decreased with time and then fluctuation, (2) through hole was observed only after the inception of fluctuation, and so on. In this work, we focused on the observation of PD properties of PP films with artificial through hole and comparison with conventional samples (without artificial through hole). As a result, (1) no discharge of the large charge band occurs, (2) polarity differences in the number of discharges and PD patterns occur, (3) the degraded range of PP film is narrower than that of the conventional sample, and (4) donut-shaped emission images are observed, which were not observed in the conventional sample. However, the fluctuation itself did not occur. The polarity difference is considered to be due to the presence of the through-hole, as compared to the conventional sample before and after the fluctuation. It was suggested that the presence of degradation products on the PP film surface and the gas atmosphere in the void also contributed to the fluctuation.

articleTitle: Assessment of Charge Behavior in Electrical Tree Tube Based on Characteristics of Partial Discharge Waveform
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Electrical trees are the final stage of an insulation degradation with partial discharge (PD). In a practical situation, a detection circuit that consists of a coupling capacitor and a detection impedance is applied to the PD measurement. The high-frequency signal associated with a PD pulse flows through a coupling capacitor and a detection impedance. Since a detection impedance is conventionally an RLC circuit having a large impedance with a certain frequency band, the observed PD signal is stretched by a transfer function of the detection circuit. For this reason, PD phenomena are not generally discussed by using PD waveform itself. It mostly investigated the occurrence time (phase) and the charge amount as the parameters; however, the original PD waveform shows the behavior of charges in the discharge space. The information on degradation characteristics can be obtained by analyzing the change of the PD waveform. In this study we constructed a device which can be acquired all the original PD waveforms. The charge behavior in the electrical trees was evaluated based on the characteristics change of the PD waveform.

articleTitle: DC Insulation Properties of Commercial Grade 320 kV HVDC XLPE/MgO Nanocomposite Material
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) nanocomposite insulations exhibit the improved electrical properties for the high voltage cable application. This paper compares the DC insulation properties of as-received 320 kV HVDC XLPE/MgO nanocomposite material with the reference to pure XLPE at 25 °C test temperature. The MgO nanofiller dispersion is analyzed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). DC breakdown strength is measured by applying the ramp voltage at a rate of 0.5 kV/s and space charge is measured at 50 kV/mm using the pulse electroacoustic system. Moreover, the test samples are exposed to the thermal aging at 135 °C for 30 days inside the hot-air oven. The fresh XLPE nanocomposite samples exhibit 20% higher DC breakdown strength and negligible hetero charge accumulation near the anode than fresh pure XLPE. The aforementioned properties of XLPE nanocomposite remain largely unaffected as compared to pure XLPE after its thermal aging. The thermal aging of pure XLPE decreases its DC breakdown strength by 38%, whereas the XLPE nanocomposite shows a 20% decrease. The thermal aging generates negligible hetero charges near the anode. However, significant hetero charges are accumulated near both electrodes after thermal aging inside the pure XLPE. The enhanced performance of the XLPE nanocomposite against thermal aging properties is attributed to its intact morphology.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Effect of Silver Sulfide on the Dielectric Properties of Mixed Insulating Liquid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In recent years, the use of mineral oil and ester fluid mixtures as a possible alternative to mineral oil has attracted the attention of many researchers. However, mixing different insulating liquids comes with many challenges requiring in-depth consideration. One of these challenges is the evaluation of the effect of silver sulfide, forming as a result of corrosive sulfur mixing with the silver layer coating on-load tap changers, on the dielectric properties of the insulating mixture. This paper addresses this issue and reports the results of an experimental investigation to evaluate the effect of adding silver sulfide with different concentration on the dielectric properties of mineral oil-ester fluid mixture. The results show that the addition of silver sulfide to the mixed liquid has reduced the inception voltage due to its semiconductive nature and induced surface charges. Flow electrification studies adopting spinning disc confirms the increase in the streaming current with disc velocity. A negative streaming current was observed in the mixed liquid on its interaction with the pressboard interface. The study also indicates that increased concentration of silver sulfide mixture showed a higher loss tangent and an increase in the streaming current. The physico-chemical properties of the oil through rheological studies observed a marginal change on the addition of silver sulfide to the mixed liquid and it correlates with the electrostatic charging tendency (ECT) of the oil.

articleTitle: Proposal of Noise Rejection in Automatic Measurement System of Repetitive Partial Discharge Inception Voltage
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Repetitive partial discharge inception voltage (RPDIV) measurement is necessary for inverter-fed motor when testing according to IEC 60034-18-41. Our previous study showed an influence of the position and distance of EM sensor on the sensitivity of detected EM wave to quantitatively evaluate RPDIV by using the RPDIV automatic measurement system. This paper deals with proposal of a new PDIV automatic measurement method for determining PDIV correctly as well as experimental confirmation with twisted pairs for the noise rejection method to work. Results reveal that the proposed algorithm improved PD and noise discrimination accuracy to reject significantly the influence of noise in determining PDIV and RPDIV by applying the repetitive impulse voltage to the sample.

articleTitle: Durability Test of Enamel Containing Nano-Cray under Artificial inverter Surge Condition for Medium and Small-Scale Generator
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: As a NEDO project, we have been developing insulation materials for small and medium-sized generators that apply nanocomposite technology. So far, new insulating materials have been developed. The prototyped enameled wire had a life of 10,000 times or more as compared with a commercially available enameled wire for partial discharge. The heat resistance of the enameled wire was 240 °C or higher, and the dielectric breakdown voltage was 100 kV/mm or higher. In addition, the general characteristics were similar to those of commercially available enameled wire. In the future, a prototype model will be manufactured to demonstrate the effect of reducing power consumption.

articleTitle: Investigation of The Effect of DC Voltage Increasing Rate on Space Charge Distribution and Dielectric Breakdown In Low Density Polyethylene
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Effect of dc voltage increasing rate for a dc breakdown test on a space charge accumulation in an insulating material was investigated. To evaluate the dc dielectric strength of a polymeric insulating material, a ramp voltage has been preferably applied to the material. However, when the dc voltage is applied to the material, a space charge accumulates in the material and it strongly affects the breakdown strength. Since the space charge accumulation characteristics are affected by the increase rate of the applied dc voltage, it is important to understand the relationship between the increase rate and the space charge accumulation behavior. In this report, we investigated the relationship between them in low-density polyethylene and modified cross-linked polyethylene for dc use as samples of the insulating materials. To observe the space charge accumulation behavior, pulsed electroacoustic method was used. Judging from the results, it was found while the rapid increase rate of the applied voltage induced a large amount of space charge accumulation in low-density polyethylene, the gradual increase rate suppressed the accumulation of it. On the other hand, it was also found that any obvious difference was not observed in the modified cross-linked polyethylene by the change of the voltage increase rate.

articleTitle: Study on the Difference of Space Charge Distribution in EPDM under DC and AC Electric Fields
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In order to compare the difference on space charge formation mechanism under DC and AC fields before and after thermal aging, the space charge behavior in Ethylene-Propylene-Diene Monomer(EPDM) is investigated in this paper. Part of the samples degassed in advance were thermal aged at 200 °C for 9 h. The space charge behavior was detected under 1~25 kV/mm DC field with polarity reversal and AC field, respectively. For unaged sample, heterocharge and homocharge appears near the top electrode with semi-conducting material and the bottom electrode with aluminum material, respectively. The heterocharge accumulation area near the top electrode narrows, while the distribution range of homocharge near the the bottom electrode expands after thermal aging at 200 °C. In the condition of AC field pressure, heterocharge and homocharge accumulates near the top electrode and the bottom electrode inside unaged sample, respectively. After thermal aging at 200 °C, the internal charge distribution of the sample tends to be consistent with the phenomenon under DC field. Based on the characteristics of charge diffusion and migration, it is inferred that the heterocharge in the unaged sample mainly originates from the dissociation of impurities, and the homocharge mainly due to the electrode injection. Thermal aging at 200 °C may weaken the impurity dissociation and enhance charge injection. Moreover, some deep traps may be introduced during thermal aging at 200 °C, resulting in a more difficult detrapping process. Compared the phenomena of space charge behavior under DC and AC fields, the differences are mainly due to the fact that the space charge inside the sample under DC field mainly comes from electrode injection, while the space charge under AC field mainly comes from impurity dissociation.

articleTitle: Breakdown Characteristics of Cone-type ε-FGM Spacer for Gas Insulated Switchgears
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: For the downsizing of gas insulated switchgears (GIS), a novel electric field grading technique is highly expected. In order to meet this demand, we have been investigating the electric field control and relaxation technique by “functionally graded materials” with the spatial distribution of permittivity (ε-FGM). In this paper, we fabricated the 1/4-sized cone-type ε-FGM spacer for 245 kV-class GIS and verified its breakdown voltage improvement effect by both experiment and simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Conductivity Characteristics of Polypropylene under Extra High Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In order to investigate the conductivity characteristics of polymer under extra high electric field, samples of polypropylene (PP) were prepared and the experiment of high field conduction current was carried out from low electric field to sample breakdown. The results show that the absorption current during relaxation process increases with the increased electric field, and the conduction current under different electric fields has obvious three-stage distribution at 2~10 kV/mm, 10~100 kV/mm, and 100–450 kV/mm, which corresponds to the space charge limited current (SCLC) theory rather than Schottky emission or field emission. A quantum chemical calculation is developed to reveal the current characteristics under different electric fields. The increase of the electric field promotes the charge transport in dipoles and increases the dipole moment of molecule, which enhances the fast charging current at the initial polarization process. Moreover, the narrowing of forbidden gap under electric field may lead to the nonlinear increase of the conduction current. Considering the space charge accumulation, the weakening of Schottky emission and the space charge migration make the SCLC account for the main conduction current under extra high electric field.

articleTitle: Optical Second Harmonic Microscope for Visualizing the Electric Field in Organic Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Double-beam SHG microscope unit has been designed and constructed to visualize the longitudinal electric field in the organic thin films. For this microscope, two laser beams were obliquely impinged on the sample surface simultaneously. Using this microscope, we tried to evaluate the electric field inside the organic thin films. We could visualize the in-plane distribution of the longitudinal electric field in the organic thin films while applying a voltage to the device.

articleTitle: Discharge Inception Characteristics Analysis of Epoxy / Silica Nanocomposites in SF6 Gas using Volume-time theory
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper reports comparison of measured results of partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) of epoxy/silica (EP/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) composites sample in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas with estimated one derived from Volume-time theory. The discussion is made to elucidate mechanism of discharge inception in the wedge gap formed between the solid insulation material and SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas. Namely, the dependence of the PD occurrence probability on the applied voltage was calculated using Volume-time theory and compared with measured one. Results show that without assuming electron emission from the solid insulator surface, the voltage dependence of the PD occurrence probability derived from the Volume-time theory agrees well with measured one at the voltage below 30 kV, while they do not match at higher voltage. Calculated results in assuming the electron emission from the solid insulator surface are also found to agree with measured ones in all the voltage region considered. This agreement demonstrates the validity of the Volume time theory that EP and EP / SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> initiate a discharge in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> by emitting initial electrons from the insulator surface as well as electron detachment from SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>- ions. These results suggest that discharge initiation can be suppressed by increasing the ionization energy by adding the SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanofiller to EP.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Change in Bow-tie Tree Degradation Due to Additional Voltage Application by Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: It is important to investigate the change in bow-tie tree degradation with voltage application to clarify the mechanism of electrical-tree inception from bow-tie tree and influence of bowtie tree degradation on electrical insulation. The present study focused on the change in bow-tie tree degradation before and after voltage application. It is often difficult compare the optical microscope images before and after voltage application objectively, as the acquisition conditions of each image are different, e.g. brightness distribution. In order to unify the brightness distribution, methods for standardizing the background brightness distributions were developed in this study. However, since most of the image data is in the background, the changes in the tree region may have been cancelled out after standardization. Therefore, two approaches were made to reconstruct the background distribution by assuming that the background brightness distribution was approximated by a normal distribution. In addition, after standardizing the created brightness distributions, we compared the shapes and methods by differential extraction before and after the application of voltage. The use of these methods together with proper setting of brightness threshold enabled to observe the bow-tie tree region. By taking the difference between the bow-tie tree images before and after voltage application, the change induced by voltage application, e.g. tree extension, was detected. These method, however, require further development, as these are not applicable in the case that these original background distribution shows prominent asymmetry.

articleTitle: Temperature-dependent Electrical and Thermal Characteristics of tpPI/h-BN Composite Insulating Material Using Electrostatic Adsorption Method
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The composite material with both a higher thermal conductivity and acceptable breakdown strength has been developed to reduce the cost and thermal conductive plate thickness. To develop a thermal conductive composite insulating material, thermoplastic polyimide (tpPI)/ hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) composite were produced by an electrostatic adsorption method, and the breakdown strength (Fb) and the thermal conductivity of the composite were measured at high temperature. The Fb under the impulse voltage application showed a constant value regardless of the measurement temperature. The thermal conductivity of the tpPI/h-BN composite at 393 K was higher than that at 303 K. The thermal property of tpPI led to the temperate dependent thermal conductivity of the composite. The fabricated tpPI/h-BN composites showed excellent electrical and thermal properties even at high temperatures.

articleTitle: Optimization of The Superhydrophobic Insulation Longevity Covered With Water Drops Under DC Voltage
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The electrical networks are confronted with several problems that lead to service disruption due to the pollution that is deposited in layer form and the persistence of water drops by the effect of moisture on hydrophobic insulators. Our experimental work aims to manufacture superhydrophobic insulation based on silicone and to control the evacuation of water droplets deposits covering the surface using a very suitable electrode profile in order to prevent the development of partial electrical discharges and/or flashover under DC voltage. The results from this experimental study show the expulsion mode of water drops out the surface requires a test voltage less than or equal to half that of its flashover. Furthermore, these results reveal that a deposit of a set of water drops on the superhydrophobic insulation, whatever their volume, their electrical conductivity, the superhydrophobicity of its surface is retained and its longevity is optimized.

articleTitle: The Study of Surface Flashover Affected by Corona Discharging via Non-invasive Surface Potential Measurement
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The corona discharge caused by the metal tip influences the surface condition of the insulator, which furtherly affects flashover development. Different from previous studies focused on the initial flashover voltage, this paper concentrated on the effect of corona discharging on flashover via the noninvasive measurement of surface potential during continuous flashover. When there was no corona discharging, positive flashover showed shorter flashover intervals (FI) and higher surface potential mutation (SPM) than negative flashover, which was mainly caused by the formation of positive charge region around high voltage electrode. Both positive and negative corona made the FI longer, indicating that the degree of corona discharge in this experiment improved the flashover resistance of the epoxy. Comprehensive analysis between the entropy of both FI and SPM interpreted the dispersivity of flashover channels. Research showed that positive corona did not affect the concentrated flashover channels of positive flashover, while negative corona significantly increased the entropy of positive flashover, manifesting that the surface defects formed by the radial negative corona provided the possibility of lateral development for the positive flashover channels. For the original dispersed channels of negative flashover, the entropy of negative flashover after corona discharging was slightly lower than the flashover without corona, illustrating the defects caused by the corona discharging fixed the formation of flashover channels.

articleTitle: Dielectric Breakdown Characteristic of Refining Treatment Fullerene Doped Epoxy Plate-like Specimens
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper presents dielectric breakdown characteristics of refining treatment fullerene doped epoxy plate samples. Three types of fullerene doped epoxy (EP) nanocomposites were prepared to investigate the effect of refining treatments in ac dielectric breakdown strength. That is, two kinds of mixed fullerenes and pure C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sub> were used as nanofillers, and neat EP was also used for comparison. As a result, it is revealed that the dielectric breakdown strength of all three types of 0.2 wt% fullerene doped EP increases by about 30% compared with that of neat EP, and the effect of the refining treatment is small under the present conditions.

articleTitle: Current Reduction Caused by Strong Local Field in Low-Density Polyethylene under Various Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper presents experimental studies on J-E characteristics and space charge distributions for a low-density polyethylene (LDPE) sheet between semi-conduction-anode and Al-cathode under high dc field. In normal cases, the steady current density J in a polymer sheet increases with increasing the mean applied field strength E. We measured the value of J under each applied field E from 0.1 to 1.5 MV/cm for the LDPE sheet under various temperatures between 30 and 60°C. The relationships between J and E for the LDPE can be expressed as J α E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> until E exceeds a threshold value E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The J-E characteristics for E <; E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> can be explained with the well-known space charge limited current (SCLC) model. However, J is reduced with increasing E when E > E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The threshold value E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> increased with increasing temperature. We confirmed that a large number of positive space charges were injected into the bulk of LDPE when E > E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. They were accumulated in the LDPE bulk, so that the local field strength near the cathode became much larger than the applied field. These results imply that the charge mobility of the space charge in the local high field area must be lower than that in the low field area. The positive charge density in the LDPE bulk was reduced with increasing temperature. The field distortion caused by the space charge accumulation in the LDPE bulk cannot be observed at 60°C. The current reduction phenomenon was not also observed at 60 °C. On the basis of these results, the reason why the charge mobility was reduced by the field concentration into the local area will be discussed.

articleTitle: Dielectric Property Measurement of Freshwater Fishes and Parasite Affecting Infection Opisthorchis Viverrini for Dielectric Heating Application
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recent works have shown that dielectric properties play an important role in distinguishing parasites from freshwater fishes. However, a few studies focus on the fishes of family Cyprinidae, which is the top cause of cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) in Thailand. In this paper, we propose to study dielectric properties for three fish types in family Cyprinidae. The main aim is to compare the differences between the dielectric properties of both the fishes and the parasites. The experiment was based on studying three fish types, with different characters, in family Cyprinidae: Common silver barb (CSB), Seven-striped barb (SC) and Bighead carp (BC). Dielectric properties measurement for head, trunk, tail and belly of the fishes were compared between the fish with scales and fish with removed scales by using frequencies at 40 MHz, 915 MHz, 1800 MHz, and 2450 MHz. The experimental results showed that the dielectric loss factor of the fish with removed scales was higher than the dielectric loss factor of the fish with scales and the dielectric loss factor of the parasites in both RF and MW. For the parasite, it can be significantly observed that the dielectric loss factor both RF and MW were higher than the dielectric loss factor of the fish with scales. This indicates this study is useful for dielectric heating application in exterminating the parasites in the fishes. This result can be applied in the future to exterminate the parasites in uncooked fish by using dielectric heating technique.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Transient Behavior of Packet-Like Space Charge in Low Density Polyethylene
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is widely used for AC electric devices and AC power cables. However, when a DC high voltage is applied to the LDPE, electric charge injection occurs. The injected space charge distorts the electric field in the LDPE. To investigate the space charge injection, we perform the simulation of the space charge injection. In the simulation, we calculate the dynamics of the space charge by taking into account the electric field dependence of the mobility. The effects of the mobility on the space charge injection depth is discussed from the electric field dependent mobility.

articleTitle: Insulation Performance of Safety-Related Electrical Penetrations for Pressurized Water Reactors under Simulated Severe Accident Conditions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Electrical penetrations (EPs) in nuclear power plants play important roles in keeping a primary containment vessel airtight and in connecting electrical cables from the inside to the outside. Safety-related EPs, which are categorized as “severe-accident (SA) equipment,” are required to maintain their intended functions under various SA environmental conditions after having been aged under the normal operating conditions throughout their service lives. To investigate the insulation performance of EPs in a SA environment, we tested two EPs that are equivalent to those used in pressurized water reactors in Japan. One EP specimen was pre-aged in a concurrent thermal and radiation environment at 100°C and 100 Gy/h for several thousand hours to simulate the degradation induced during the designated service period. The other EP specimen was used without pre-aging. To simulate the degradation induced by radiation during a SA, the EPs were irradiated with gamma rays to a total dose of 500 kGy at a dose rate of 7 kGy/h. Subsequently, the EP specimens were exposed to saturated steam at 155°C and 0.45 MPaG for 168 h. The electrical insulation resistance between the insulated cores of cables in each EP specimen were monitored during the steam exposure. The minimum insulation resistances that we measured during the steam exposure for EP specimens with and without the pre-aging are about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>Ω, respectively, confirming that they retain sufficiently good insulation performance.

articleTitle: Surface and Internal Charge Measurement in Fluorinated Polymer Irradiated by Electron Using Non-contact Type PEA Method Measurement Apparatus
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Spacecrafts are exposed by the radioactive rays, such as high energy electrons and protons, plasma. The surface insulating materials of spacecraft are charged because of exposing by such high energy charged particles. This charging phenomenon is the origin of the electrostatic discharge and may lead to the fatal error of those operations. For the improving the reliability of spacecraft operation, we should understand charge accumulation phenomena based on the real surface condition. Therefore, our grope and other researchers have tried to develop systems to measure the surface and bulk charges of materials. As the results, we developed new space charge measurement equipment using the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) method. That system can apply the pulsed electric filed to the sample through the vacuum gap using a grid electrode located 125 μm above the sample. Electrons through the grid electrode to the sample. Therefore, this apparatus can measure the surface and internal charge accumulation in the bulk of materials. Although we had measured only internal charge accumulation by the conventional PEA method, we obtained a seamless charge profile from the surface to internal of the sample by such newly developed system. In this report, we measured space charge distribution in the fluorinated materials by above developed system under electron irradiation. We found the following results. The negative charge accumulation distributed from the irradiation surface to penetration depth in the bulk. The amount of irradiated electrons accumulation was more than 30 times as much as the results obtained by a conventional measurement system. From those results, the space charge distribution has been able to measure under conditions consistent with close to actual use.

articleTitle: Development of Stretchable Devices Using Multi-layer Organic Materials
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Stretchability is a fundamental requirement for nonplanar electronic devices such as a health monitoring system attached to a human body, or a solar cell attached to cylindrical/spherical buildings. Generally, flexible electronic devices can be achieved by laminating thin films of functional materials on a flexible substrate, as thin films are usually resistive to bending deformation. On the other hand, stretchable electronic devices are difficult to fabricate, because stretch is inevitably applied to the components of electronic devices. In this study, as a way of making stretchable electronic devices, we attached a thin film of organic electronic material onto an elastomeric substrate resulting in a wavy pattern on the surface. By utilizing the plastic deformation of a thin film, a wavy pattern of an organic material can be achieved in a simple manner, which exhibits stretchability by flattening its structure under stretch.

articleTitle: Tuning the Luminescent Intensity by Controlling the Distance Between Gold Quantum Dots and Silver Nanoprisms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Plasmonic nanostructures can be used to control the photoluminescence properties of several photoluminescence materials. In this work, an efficient plasmon-induced energy transfer (quenching) was investigated. The luminescent intensity of gold quantum dots (AuQDs) was controlled by the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of silver nanoprisms (AgNPrs). Since the quenching effect of this system depended on the distance between AuQDs and AgNPrs, the difference chain lengths of alkanedithiol molecules were used to control the distance between those nanomaterials. The 69% quenching of AuQDs was observed when 1,6-hexanedithiol-functionalized AgNPrs acted as a quencher. When AgNPrs with a longer chain length of alkanedithiol was used as a quencher, the decrease in quenching efficiency was observed. These were due to the effect of fluorescence resonance energy transfer. This technique was utilized for detection of bovine serum albumin with the detection limit of 10 ng/mL.

articleTitle: Effect of Ethanol Concentration on Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae Sterilization by High Electric Field Pulse Application
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The sterilization method using a high electric field pulse is attracting attention as a new sterilization technique for liquid foods because the method does not change the nutrient of liquid foods. Many researchers reported that high electric field pulse application killed a lot of types of bacteria in liquid foods. In the process of alcoholic beverages (Japanese sake), non-thermal sterilization is wildly used to get good quality. The high-temperature changes the smell and composition of alcoholic beverages. In this study, the targets of sterilization ware Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae. We studied the effect of ethanol concentration on the killing of Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae using high electric field pulse application.

articleTitle: Surface Modification of Nano-BaTiO3 by Perfluorosilane Coupling Agent and its Effects on Dielectric Properties of High-k Photosensitive Composites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this paper, using 1H, 1H, 2H, 2H-perfluorooctyltrimethoxysilane (FAS-17) to modify BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanoparticles, UV-cured resin composites with different contents of nano-BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> were prepared. The modified nanoparticles were characterized by FT-IR and XPS. The effects of surface-treated BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanoparticles on the dielectric constant, dielectric loss, volume resistivity and breakdown strength of composites were investigated. The results show that the molecule of FAS-17 is successfully grafted onto the surface of nano-BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. Compared with the unmodified composite, the dielectric constant of photosensitive composite filled with modified nano-BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> was slightly reduced, and the dielectric loss was dramatically reduced. Moreover, the volume resistivity and AC breakdown strength of modified nanocomposites were significantly improved. The forming of H-bonding and additional interfacial traps are beneficial to the improved dispersion of nano-fillers in the matrix and the restricted mobility of free electrons, which are responsible for the significantly enhanced dielectric properties.

articleTitle: Effect of Magnetic and Non-magnetic Nanoparticles on Insulation and Cooling Behaviour of a Natural Ester for Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper analyses and compares the impact that maghemite and titania nanoparticles have in the electrical and thermal performance of a commercial natural ester used in power transformers. Vegetal-oil-based nanofluids have been prepared at different concentrations. Once the nanofluids were obtained, the breakdown voltage of the oil samples with and without nanoparticles was measured. It was found that the concentration of nanoparticles influences the breakdown voltage of natural ester. The existence of optimal concentrations has been noticed, and these nanofluids were selected for the upcoming tests. The cooling capacity of these liquids and the base fluid was measured through a thermal analysis in an experimental platform. The experiment developed is based on a 1-phase transformer (800 VA, 230/115 V) immersed in a stainless-steel fulfilled with insulating liquid. The temperatures inside the tank were monitored at the bottom and at the top of the tub to measure the oil temperature. Other sensor measured the hotspot winding temperature, defined as the hottest temperature of winding conductors in contact with solid insulation or insulating liquid. This sensor was located at the top of the winding as the most probable hot-spot location. Ambient temperature was also measured as a reference. A microcontroller (Arduino) and an Integrated Development Environment (IDE) was utilized to record the measurements of the sensors. The results of the thermal study showed that only maghemite based nanofluids exhibited improved heat transfer characteristics in comparison with the natural ester oil.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Noise and DC Offset Voltage on Signal Processing for Space Charge Measurement of HVDC Cables
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The influences of noise and DC offset voltage on the maximum electric field, root-mean-square error (RMSE) of space charge profile, and RMSE of the electric field profile in insulating materials, such as HVDC cables, are evaluated using a signal processing method and a reference waveform. Also, baseline correction was used to rectify errors. Based on the noise evaluation, the maximum of three-sigma intervals at S/N ratio +20 dB was 19 % for the maximum electric field, 7.5 % for RMSE of the electric field profile, and 10.6 % for RMSE of space charge profile with baseline correction. The maximum electric field is affected twice as much by the noise level, compared to the other parameters. Based on the DC offset voltage evaluation, a DC offset voltage of ±1% could introduce a 23 % relative error into the maximum electric field without baseline correction and a 6.6 % relative error in the maximum electric field with baseline correction. Hence, it was found that baseline correction reduces ±1% DC offset voltage error by 16 %.

articleTitle: Dielectrophoretic Devices Fabricated by Proton Beam Writing for Concentration, Assembly, and Detection of Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Dielectrophoresis (DEP) is a phenomenon with directional movement of micro particles due to the DEP force under uneven AC electric field. We utilize polymer surface with microstructures such as μm-scale pit arrays for DEP devices to assemble or concentrate nanoparticles. For micro-structuring of the polymer such as PMMA with thickness of 5-10 μm, we applied proton beam writing (PBW) which is a direct-write lithographic technique for high-aspect ratio microstructures of polymeric materials such as PMMA and epoxy resin. Pit arrays such as 5 x 5 arrays of circular pits with diameter of 5 μm on the 5-10 μm thick PMMA. We were able to demonstrate collection and assembly of gold and Ag nanoparticles (diameter of 100 to 250 nm) on the PMMA pit arrays from the colloidal suspension of the metallic nanoparticles in water. The DEP experiments were performed with the amplitude (10-20 V) and frequency (1-100 kHz) of applied ac voltages with additional dc offset voltage of less than 1V. We also discuss possible application of this technique to the detection of micro and nanoparticles such as plastics, dielectrics and metals in environmental water.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Fault Localization of Semiconductor Devices with Ultrasound Heating
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: As a conventional alternative, the IR-OBIRCH method is widely used to localize faults in semiconductor devices. In the IR-OBIRCH, the faults are localized by observing current changes induced by laser heating. Since the mold resin is not optically transparent and it disturbs the propagation of laser, the IR-OBIRCH method often requires a decapsulation of mold resin prior to the localization of the faults. The engineers of semiconductor devices call for a new alternative without need for the decapsulation which can find out where the circuit was broken down by an overvoltage. The authors developed the SOBIRCH method as an alternative without need for the decapsulation of mold resin. Today, semiconductor devices are in a trend of having a structure of stacked LSI chips by three-dimensional integration technology. By using a sample with simplified stacked structure of three-dimensional integration, this report suggested a possibility that the ultrasound resonance improves the sensitivity of SOBIRCH in cases of three-dimensional integrated semiconductor devices having a stacked structure.

articleTitle: Innovative Functional Insulating Materials Development for Advanced Electric Power Apparatuses Outline of NEDO Project
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A project titled “Technological development of innovative functional insulation materials for electric power equipment” is adopted for a Strategic Energy-saving Technological Innovation Program/theme setting Business Cooperation Scheme in the fiscal year of 2017 in NEDO (New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization). This research project officially started in September 2017 and lasts till the fiscal year of 2021. The theme of this development is nanocomposite technology in which polymer resin and inorganic nanomaterials are compounded, and functionally gradient material (FGM) in which dielectric constant and resistivity are graded by compounding with inorganic nano or micro fillers. This project aims to develop a high-performance insulating material that could not be realized on the conventional extension line. This article introduces the future prospects from the background, purpose, outline, and contents of the research and development of this project.

articleTitle: Understanding the Space Charge variation in Silicone rubber with different Low Molecular Weight Siloxanes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The low molecular weight (LMW) siloxanes play major role in Silicone Rubber (SR) insulators to get better hydrophobicity and hydrophobicity recovery characteristics over contaminated surface of the insulators in outdoor environment. The surface and bulk properties of the n-hexane treated SR composites were analyzed by various experimental studies. The reduction in hydrophobicity of SR samples after nhexane treatment was observed due to extraction of LMW siloxanes. The higher contact angle was observed in filler SR samples after extraction due to strong interfacial regions between filler and polymer matrix, where the loss of LMW siloxanes were less. From the FTIR studies, a small reduction in methyl and siloxanes functional groups was observed after nhexane treatment, resulting in the reduction of hydrophobicity of the specimens. The enhanced space charge accumulation was observed after n-hexane treatment compared to untreated one, where the least increment of space charge density is observed in S3 sample.

articleTitle: Addition Effect of Nitrogen Fine Bubbles and Nonionic Polymer Surfactant to Pure Water on Resistivity and Negative Lightning Impulse Breakdown Voltage of Pure Water
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: We have been investigating electrical properties of pure water as one of new liquid insulation materials with environmentally friendly excellent insulation performance. However, if pure water is used as liquid insulating material, there is a disadvantage to increase power loss, because pure water has a lower resistivity than insulating oils. Therefore, it is necessary to increase the resistivity of pure water. In our previous studies, it was confirmed that the resistivity increased when specific nonionic polymer surfactants (nonionic polymers) or nitrogen fine bubbles (N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs) were individually added to pure water. In this paper, we investigated the addition effect of nitrogen fine bubbles and nonionic polymer surfactant to pure water on resistivity and the lightning impulse breakdown voltage (BDV) of pure water. As a result, the resistivity of pure water to which N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs were added (pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs) was approximately 1.7 MΩ·cm. On the other hand, the maximum value of the resistivity of each pure water to which N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs and nonionic polymer were added simultaneously (pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs and nonionic polymer) was approximately 1.8 MΩ·cm. The resistivity of each pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs and nonionic polymer was almost equal to the resistivity of pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs. The 50% BDV of pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs was approximately -75 kV. On the other hand, the 50% BDVs of each pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs and nonionic polymer were approximately -50 to -60 kV. The BDVs of each pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs and nonionic polymer were lower than that of pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs, which was the same as that 50% BDV of pure water. Assuming that polymers adsorbed at the fine bubble interface since polymers adsorbed at the gas-liquid interface, it can be explained as below. It is possible that each pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs and nonionic polymer may have been the same resistivity as pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs because the nonionic polymer attached around N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs and there may be few nonionic polymers floating alone. It is also considered that pure water added with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs and nonionic polymer have been insulation weaknesses because the nonionic polymer was adsorbed to N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-FBs to form clusters.

articleTitle: Special Behaviors of Space Charge inside Insulating Materials under Different Polarization Conditions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper reports the space charge characteristics of insulating materials under DC and square wave voltages with different parameters. By using the pulsed electro-acoustic method, the effect of polarization conditions on charge accumulation and electric field distortion inside polyimide insulation is compared and analyzed. The experimental results find that the accumulated positive charge amount and electric field distortion under some square wave conditions are much larger than those under DC voltages. It also shows a polarity effect of charge accumulation under positive and negative square waves with different frequencies. As a result, the maximum electric field strengths under the two conditions appear at 10 Hz and 500 Hz, respectively. The measured results under the square waves with different amplitudes further confirm that the problem of charge accumulation and electric field distortion is more serious under negative ones. The results in this paper can provide guidance for the actual application and further improvement of polyimide materials under square wave conditions.

articleTitle: Carbonization Phenomena Dependence on Pressure between Insulation Sheets by Steeper Inverter Surge at Inverter Fed Motor
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recently, “carbonization phenomena on the insulation sheets” were newly detected as the unique precursor phenomena to the burning of the insulation of inverter-fed motors due to leakage current through the insulation system. We have previously studied the generation condition for the high dV/dt resulting in an inverter surge. In this study, we built an experimental setup based on an elemental model to simulate a steep surge voltages in the inverter and constructed the stator insulation inside the motor core to control the pressure between the insulation sheets. This paper reports the carbonization characteristics and the insulation design to prevent the carbonization caused by steep inverter surges.

articleTitle: Effect of High Current Pulses on Germinability of Radish Sprout Seeds
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study on promotion of germination of radish sprout seeds (Kaiware daikon) with two kinds of pulsed power technique, dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) in air and high current pulse (HCP) in water. The germination rate after 4-days cultivation at 25 °C in a blight room is only 30 % for the seeds without any electrical stimulations because the radish sprout seeds are photophobic, so called negatively photoblastic seeds. The germination rate of the seeds under illumination significantly increases with increasing the DBD treatment time. The germination rate is up to 70 % by 30-min-DBD and further up to 90 % by 60-min-DBD. In this study, we confirm that the germination rate is also improved by the HCP treatment. Very short current pulses of 80 A are applied to the seeds in tap water between plane-plane electrodes. However, the germination rate of the seeds subjected to the HCP is lower than that subjected to the DBD. The germination rate is 60 % for 30-min-HCP and it is also 60 % for 60-min-HCP. The difference in the mechanism of the sprout promotion between the DBD and the HCP treatments will be discussed.

articleTitle: A Study on the Behavior of Interfacial Space Charge at Polymer Dielectric Double-Layer Simulating the HVDC Cable Joints
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this study, the characteristics of the space charge at the interface inside the cable joints known as the weak part of the HVDC cable were experimentally identified. For the experiment, a double-layer sample was made of two types of polymer and after applying a DC voltage, the space charge at the interface was measured and analyzed. The polarity of the space charge formed at the interface was consistent with the Maxwell-Wagner model. The time dependence of space charge accumulation and disappearance will be further studied through additional experiments and analysis in the future.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Characteristics of Mineral Oil Immersed Transformer Compared with Natural Ester and Palm Oil Immersed Transformer under Different Periods of Impregnation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper represents the partial discharge (PD) characteristics of mineral oil immersed transformer compared with natural ester, and palm oil immersed transformer under different periods of impregnation. Three identical three-phase transformers with 22kV/400V 50 kVA rated were designed and constructed. The first transformer was fully filled with mineral oil. The second transformer was fully filled with natural ester (FR3), and the third transformer was fully filled with palm oil. The partial discharge at 1.1Urated of these transformers with various conditions, i.e., non-impregnated paper, impregnated paper with 3 hours, and 6 hours was investigated. The impregnation process was done with 65 °C liquid temperature and 5 mmbar pressure. From the test results, it can be concluded that PD characteristics of the mineral oil immersed transformer was obviously different compared with these of the natural oil (FR3) immersed transformer and the palm oil immersed transformer. Moreover, the impregnation impacted PD characteristics of the tested transformers, which were analyzed and reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Space Charge and Breakdown Characteristics of XLPE/BNNSs Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Cross linked polyethylene (XLPE) has the excellent insulation properties, but which is easy to accumulate space charge under the electric field owing to its low thermal conductivity. Boron nitride nanosheets (BNNSs) with high thermal conductivity were introduced into XLPE matrix to improve the thermal conductivity and electrical properties of the composite. XLPE/BNNSs nanocomposites were prepared by the melt blending method. The basic characteristics of nanoparticles and composite samples were characterized by FTIR and SEM. Space charge and DC breakdown characteristics of XLPE/BNNSs nanocomposites were studied. The experimental results indicated that the introduction of BNNSs suppressed the accumulation of space charge and enhanced the DC breakdown strength of dielectric. The space charge accumulation in the XLPE/BNNSs nanocomposites was significantly reduced and the charge amounts in the material were 0.67×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup>C and 0.71x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup>C with doping concentration of 0.1 wt% and 0.5wt%. With the increase of doping concentration, the inhibition effect of space charge in the composite weakened. This is mainly due to the formation of deep traps at the interface between the electrode and the composite material, forming a “charge barrier effect” that suppressed charge injection. With the concentration increases, the “charge barrier effect” becomes weakened and charge amounts in the material increased. In addition, the breakdown strength of the XLPE/BNNSs nanocomposites first increases and then decreases with the increase of BNNSs concentration. When BNNSs concentration was 0.5wt%, the DC breakdown strength of XLPE/BNNSs composite reaches the 403.8 kV/mm, which is about 31% higher than that of pure XLPE. This is mainly because the interaction zone between XLPE matrix and nano filler captures a large number of charge carriers and inhibits the carrier transport.

articleTitle: Investigating the characteristic properties of Epoxy Nickel nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Epoxy nickel nanocomposites were prepared. Water droplet initiated Corona inception voltage (CIV) on epoxy nanocomposites were obtained through Ultra high frequency (UHF) technique, under AC and DC voltages. The discharge signal generated due to water droplet initiated discharge has dominant frequency content at around 1 GHz. CIV and contact angle increases with addition of nickel nano filler percentage in epoxy. Laser induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) gives the elemental composition in the polymer matrix and plasma temperature variation is calculated. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) studies were carried at different frequencies. It shows an increase in storage modulus and reduction in loss modulus with nanocomposites. The activation energy and the glass transition temperatures shows better value for 3wt% of nano nickel in epoxy resin.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Electrical Properties of Modified Graphene Oxide/Epoxy Composites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The interface area of a dielectric material is a key factor affecting the dielectric properties of the material. Directly observing and analyzing the electrical characteristics of the interface is a challenge. In order to study the role of interface area on a microscopic scale, the experimental platform of fixed-point charge injection technique was built around an individual modified GO particle embedded in the epoxy(EP) matrix, and the surface charge dissipation process of pure EP and GO/EP nanocomposite after fixed-point positive and negative charge injection was observed and studied by Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM), which indicates that the same charge accumulate at the interface, and pure EP has better ability to limit charge than nanocomposite.

articleTitle: Optimization of Partial Discharge Detection Sensitivity of Transient Earth Voltage Sensors Using FDTD Modeling
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) measurement provides early warning information for assessing the condition of high voltage (HV) power equipment insulation systems, so maintenance can be taken to prevent service interruption due to isolation failures. Many methods and sensors have been tried and developed to detect PD. PD produces electromagnetic waves that can be detected using transient earth voltage (TEV) sensors. The TEV sensor is small, and it can be easily used by attaching the sensor to the metal casing of power equipment in several positions. This paper presents the optimization of TEV sensor by electromagnetic wave propagation simulation using three-dimension finite difference time domain (FDTD) modeling. The simulation was made with a three-dimension finite difference time domain (FDTD) simulation software (CTC Co.; MAGNA TDM version 8.3). The structure of newly proposed TEV sensor is optimized for partial discharge measurement in terms of a more compact physical construction and simpler to manufacture. The TEV sensor structure was developed and optimized using the FDTD software domain before the physical sensor was tested. The approach in this paper will help to make TEV sensor designs more compact in certain applications in the future.

articleTitle: Charge Behavior Measurement near the Interface Parallel to the Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: It is important to understand the charge behavior in a multilayer insulation system in which the electric field direction is parallel to the interface because the interface may become an electrically weak point. The electric charge behavior measurement near the interface in the multilayer insulation system in which the electric field direction is parallel to the interface was carried out in this paper using a current integral charge method. The accumulated charge amount of the detection capacitor in the multilayer insulation system with the interface showed the trend to increase under a low field application compared to that of the single-layer without the interface. The interface in the multilayer insulation system acted as an electrically weak point under the experimental condition, the charge traveled to the counter electrode through the vicinity of the interface or accumulated near the interface. The current integral charge method may be a powerful tool to understand the charge behavior.

articleTitle: Electric Field Grading by Permittivity and Conductivity Graded Materials (ε/σ-FGM) for HVDC Gas Insulated Power Apparatus
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The progressive development of HVDC transmission system has urged us to develop a novel technique in supporting the performance of DC power apparatus. Functionally Graded Materials (FGM) are one of the techniques that allows us to control the electric field within the DC insulation system. Our previous work has reported that FGM with spatial conductivity distribution applied to a 320 kV DC-GIS spacer could reduce the maximum electric field under DC steady state condition. This paper investigates the applicability of the combination of spatial permittivity and conductivity graded materials (ε/σ-FGM) in DC power apparatus. ε/σ-FGM are revealed to be more effective in suppressing maximum electric field as well as more uniformly distributed electric field against the increase of temperature distribution under polarity reversal, DC-on, and impulse superimposed on DC condition.

articleTitle: Detection Using Frequency Domain Reflectometry of the Permittivity Change in a Cable Induced by the Exposure to Steam
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The fault location method that the authors are developing possesses a very high spatial resolution. If the characteristic impedance of a cable is changed, for whatever reason, the location method can find its position. In other words, this method can detect the changes in characteristic impedance. Since the characteristic impedance is a function of the permittivity of the cable insulation, this method can detect the change in permittivity of the insulation non-destructively without disassembling the cable. This paper demonstrates the above, taking a 30-m coaxial cable and a 2.5-m safety-related cable for use in a nuclear power plant as two typical examples.

articleTitle: Examination of Impulse PD Inception Location by Electric Field Analysis in Ester Oil/Pressboard Composite Insulation System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper investigates partial discharge (PD) starting point under impulse voltage application in the ester oil /press-board (PB) composite insulation system. Experimental results are compared with those in the mineral oil and PB composite system to discuss the difference of the discharge characteristics and its mechanism. For ester oil, unlike mineral oil, when the gap length was increased from 0.8 to 1.6 mm, there was no change in the distribution of the PD starting points.

articleTitle: Colorimetric Probe Based on Destabilization of Silver Nanoparticles from Polysaccharide Matrix for Creatinine Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Colorimetric probes for creatinine detection using metal nanoparticles have attracted much attention due to their unique optical properties that could be observed by UV-vis spectrometer or naked eye. In this work, starch-stabilized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were adopted for creatine detection. AgNPs were synthesized by chemical technique. Soluble starch was used as a stabilizer. AgNPs could be stabilized in starch due to steric hindrance. Creatinine is a chemical that strongly bind with AgNPs. When creatinine was mixed with starch-stabilized AgNPs, the ligand-exchange reaction of creatinine and hydroxyl groups of starch occurred and AgNPs were destabilized from polysaccharide matrix of starch. After AgNPs were destabilized from starch, free AgNPs were aggregated due to Van der Waals attraction force. Extinction spectrum of AgNP colloidal solution showed a broad spectrum and the color of solution turned to orange. This system is a unique system because the this effect cannot observe from starch-stabilized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). This work shows a high possibility to utilize AgNPs as a colorimetric probe for blood creatinine and urinary creatinine detections.

articleTitle: Aging Behavior of Soft and Hard Epoxy Resins in Simulated Nuclear-Power-Plant Environments
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Two kinds of bis-phenol epoxy resins, a soft one (SE) and a hard one (HE), were aged thermally with and without simultaneous irradiation of gamma rays. For each resin, glass transition temperature (Tg), thermal decomposition temperature, elongation at break, tensile strength, and flexural modulus were measured. The difference in Tg between SE and HE is significant, which exerts certain influences on their degradation properties. When aged, SE becomes hard and it is crosslinked, regardless of whether the simultaneous irradiation was given or not. Finally, SE becomes brittle. In contrast, the mechanical properties of HE are scarcely affected by the two aging processes. However, HE finally becomes hard if aged thermally, while it is decomposed by the irradiation.

articleTitle: A Novel On-Line Monitoring System for Diagnostics Parameters of EHV GIS Electrical Apparatuses of Transmission Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The requirements of high standards for power quality and the need of reducing the maintenance costs have shifted the paradigm of the asset management into a condition-based approach. A correct assessment leads to undertake the proper decision and thus to run the assets at their best. This requires the knowledge of many parameters related to the status. Each parameter singularly or the combination of multiple parameters allow gathering the necessary information for effective and efficient decision making. Focusing on the Transmission networks, each decision about maintenance and operation has a huge cost impact, therefore justifying the adoption of means able to simplify such decisions. One of such means is the capability of performing the on-line assessment of the conditions of an electrical apparatus by means of a monitoring system providing real-time information [1].

articleTitle: Impulse Flashover Characteristics of Cone-Type Insulating Spacer for GIS Fabrication Using Nano- micro Composites or Grading Functional Materials
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: To investigate the possibility of miniaturization of a cone-type insulating spacer of gas-insulated switchgear (GIS), flashover voltage (FOV) characteristic by standard lightning impulse voltage in the SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas were studied by fabricating mini-model spacers applying nano-micro composite (NMC) materials or ε functionally graded materials (ε-FGM). This paper reports the results of each examination. For NMC materials, epoxy resin filled with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> micro-filler (MC) was filled with 1 vol % of nanofiller (SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, SrTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) to fabricated a 1/4 size cone-type insulating spacer, and the FOV in the SF6 gas was measured. In the case of negative impulse voltage, the scale parameter (η) of the Weibull distribution of the FOV was the same as that of the MC, but the shape parameter (m) decreased in the NMC. On the other hand, the FOV under positive impulse voltage of NMC materials filled with nTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and nSrTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> increased by 12 % and 20 %, respectively, compared to that of the MC (without nano-filler).
