For the ε-FGM, a similar 1/4 size cone-type insulating spacer was fabricated, and the FOV was measured. ε-FGMs with relative permittivities (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>) between 12 and 4 were designed and fabricated using SrTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=332) and SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=4) micro-fillers. At the same time, a model with a permittivity ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=4 (uniform) was fabricated using only SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> microfillers for comparison. The FOV at 0.5 MPa-abs under a negative impulse voltage of ε-FGM spacer is higher than that of a uniform sample by approximately 23 %. Thus, both NMC and ε-FGM can improve the insulating properties of the cone-type insulating spacer.

articleTitle: The Influence of Water Aging on Dielectric and Space Charge Behaviour of MgO filled Epoxy Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In the present study the epoxy nanocomposites are water aged- dried and the cyclic process was repeated for two cycles. The % of water uptake at the point of saturation has maximum values of approximately 2.5 and 1.5 % for first and second round of aging respectively, followed by water diffusion coefficient were calculated for 0, 1, 3 and 5 wt% MgO filled epoxy nanocomposites. The results indicates that the % of water uptake was decreased for all the samples during second cycle. 3wt% MgO filled nanocomposite showed optimum % of water uptake. The dielectric properties of unaged and water aged MgO filled epoxy nanocomposites were studied using dielectric spectroscopy and compared with the neat epoxy. The real permittivity (ε`) of the nanocomposites showed increased permittivity on water diffusion to the bulk material. The space charge behavior of unaged and water aged specimens were carried out by using PEA studies. Water aged samples has showed faster space charge decay. Also, the accumulated space charge density was high with water aged specimens. Also the local electric field variation is reduced in the second cycle of water ageing.

articleTitle: Microwave Detection Technology for Internal Defects of Composite Post Insulators
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Composite post insulators are prone to internal defects due to leakage current during the operation and harsh outdoor conditions. Microwave detection is an effective nondestructive testing method. The propagation of microwave at the insulating material interface is affected by the dielectric properties of the media. The composite post insulator is a multi-interface structure and has more interfaces when there are defects inside. Therefore, the reflected microwave of the composite post insulators can be analyzed to evaluate the internal interfaces distribution of the sample. We study the propagation law of microwaves in composite post insulators and proposes a defect detection method. The method converts reflected microwaves into energy signals and compares them with reference values. A portable microwave detection equipment is designed. The device can realize the generation, detection, and processing of microwave signals. It is equipped with software for data analysis and data visualization. The sample with debonding defects on site was collected and the nonconductive defect, semiconductive defects, and conductive defect were artificially produced. The effectiveness of the detection method and the device was verified by experiments with the defects inside the sample.

articleTitle: Micro-structuring of PVDF-TrFE by Proton Beam Writing for Tactile Sensors
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Aiming at micro-structuring of Polyvinylidene fluoride trifluoroethylene (PVDF-TrFE) film for sensing applications, we studied effects of proton beam irradiation and subsequent alkaline etching processes using potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution. Dependence of the pattering depth and linewidth on the beam energy, fluence, and etching time was investigated. The depth of pattering is mainly determined by etching time for PBW with beam energy of a few MeV and with fluence of less than 10 μC/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. By using a moderate fluence of 3.0 μC/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and etching time of 3 h with beam energy of 1.7 MeV, we obtained 4 x 4 arrays of 40 μm height pillars with aspect ratio of about 5.

articleTitle: “Iontronics” Electrochemistry of biodevices
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In life science and biotechnology, we have developed biotechnologies for studying biological functions electronically, and we have developed this technology to make the best use of the various functions of living organisms to help human life and environmental conservation. It goes without saying that ions play an important role and role in biotechnology. Biosensors are one of the chemical compartmental measurement methods that apply the advanced substance recognition function of living organisms, but are also attracting attention as a step leading to molecular devices and biodevices. From these points of view, we introduce a highly durable biosensor using electrochemical detection method that we have studied on the research aiming at the enhancement of the function of the biosensor.

articleTitle: Effect of Mechanical Tensile on Nonlinear Conductivity of Silicon Carbide/Silicone Rubber Composites for Prefabricated Joint of HVDC Cable
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Field grading materials (FGMs) with nonlinear conductivity, which can uniform a local direct-current (dc) electric field, have potential applications in HVDC cable joints and terminals. For the prefabricated cable joint, an interface pressure between the main insulation (XLPE) and joint insulation (SiR) is mandated to avoid the insulation failure caused by surface flashover. Therefore, the nonlinear conductive insulation in prefabricated cable joints is maintained in an expanded state in practical application. This paper focuses on the effect of the mechanical tensile on the nonlinear conductivity characteristics in silicon carbide (SiC)/silicone rubber (SiR) composites. A three-electrode system is employed to measure the dc conductivity (σ) of SiC/SiR composites with a stretching ratio of 0 to 60% under 1-30 kV/mm, and the nonlinear coefficients are further calculated by the logE-logσ curves, respectively. The results show that when the SiC mass fraction is 90%, the conductivity and nonlinear coefficient of the sample increase with the increase of stretching ratio from 0% to 20%. However, when the stretching ratio increases further, the conductivity and nonlinear coefficient decrease. An electromechanical coupling model of SiC/SiR composites is established by using COMSOL Multiphysics. The effect of the mechanical tensile on the nonlinear conductivity is contributed to the varied conducting routes under the elastic strain of SiC/SiR composites. The doping content of SiC is related to the density of the conducting route in the composites. The higher the SiC content, the lower the sensitivity of the conducting paths to the strain, and the less sensitivity of nonlinear conductivity to the tensile strain.

articleTitle: Influence of Thermal Ageing on the Optical Performance of XLPE Cable Insulation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) is widely used as insulating material of high voltage power cables due to its excellent physicochemical and electrical properties. It is necessary to understand the thermal ageing of XLPE in order to guarantee the reliability of power cables. In this paper, the XLPE samples were subjected to thermal ageing at 155°C in air. The influence of thermal ageing on optical properties of XLPE and its structural origin were investigated by Ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometer (UV-Vis) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). It was observed that the color of XLPE samples changed from transparent white to yellow even red with ageing time. The UV-Vis absorption spectra showed that the absorption edge shifted from ultraviolet to visible region which was consistent with the color change. The optical band gap Eg calculated from UV-Vis curves was found to decrease after thermal ageing. The modification in optical properties of XLPE was attributed to the formation of conjugated clusters according to UV-Vis and FTIR results. FTIR spectra showed that the unsaturation and carbonyl groups increased with ageing time which contributes to the formation of conjugated cluster. The structural changes indicated the chain scission and oxidation of XLPE molecular chains by thermal ageing. These experimental results also provide a promising method for condition assessment of XLPE cable insulation based on optical properties of XLPE.

articleTitle: 3D Fluid Dynamic Simulation of Insulation Spacer with Graded Permittivity for GIS
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Spacers with graded permittivity enable a decrease in the diameter of gas-insulated switchgears. Distribution of epoxy-based composite materials (resins) with different permittivities dominate the permittivity gradient in spacers. High-permittivity resins, mixtures of high/low-permittivity resins at various mixing ratios, and low-permittivity resins were continuously injected to form spacers. In order to acquire permittivity distribution, viscosities of resins needed to improved. This paper compares resin injected spacers with simulation. In these spacers, both experiment and simulation showed similar tendencies of resin distribution.

articleTitle: Effect of Quenching Treatment on Morphology and Properties of Eco-friendly Polypropylene Copolymer for Cable Insulation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) based cable insulating material has raised great attention due to the recyclability and superior dielectric properties. In this paper, isotactic PP (iPP) as a common commercial PP and ethylene-propylene copolymer (EPC) with natural cooling(-2°C/min) and quenching process (- 90°C/min) were prepared to investigate the role of quenching on morphology and properties of iPP and EPC. It is found that the elongation at break of quenched iPP and EPC significantly increased by 105% and 121%, respectively. In addition, the breakdown strength of iPP decrease 6% while that of EPC increase 13% after quenching treatment. It is shown by XRD results that β-crystal is introduced in both quenched iPP and EPC specimens. The parallel lamellas of β-crystal will slide under the external force, which can result in the increased elongation at break. Moreover, the crystallinity of quenched iPP decreased by 14%, which can cause the expansion of amorphous regions and free volume. The energy accumulation of carriers under applied electric field will be significantly enhanced, which can result in the decreased breakdown strength. As for quenched EPC, non-crystallizable ethylene-propylene copolymer segments tends to be restricted in limited dimensions to form dispersed amorphous microspheres. Deep traps which are introduced by rubber microspheres are considered to be an important reason for the increased breakdown strength.

articleTitle: Space Charge Behavior of Oil-paper Insulation in Transformer Under AC Fields
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The relationship of space charge behavior and aging degree of oil-paper insulation is investigated in this paper. The insulation paper was obtained from different windings of a decommissioned transformers with three different voltage levels, i.e. 10 kV, 35 kV and 110 kV. The windings were coaxial placed, where the 10kV level winding was innermost and the 110 kV level winding was outermost. The insulation papers were vacuum dried to eliminate the influence of aging oil and then impregnated into the unaged oil. The space charge behavior under 5 kV/mm AC field was detected by a detection system based on the automatic equal phase shift (AEPS) principle. It shows that the space charge polarity inside the sample is consistent with the polarity of the semi-conductive electrode under AC field. The phase corresponding to the charge density peak lag the voltage phase by an angle. This hysteresis phenomenon is most obvious in the middle layer insulation, and the outer layer is the weakest. It seems that the positive charges are more difficult to detrap than negative charges after the voltage polarity reversion. Compared with heat dissipation condition of the outer layer insulation, the inner layer and middle layer have poor heat dissipation. More traps may be generated during thermal aging due to high temperature for inner layer and middle layer. More injected charge may be trapped with the increase of trap density, leading to the charge hysteresis phenomenon. Thus, thermal stress may have a stronger aging effect on oil-paper insulation and more attention should be paid to heat dissipation in transformer design.

articleTitle: Impact of Ultraviolet Irradiation on Space Charge Dynamics and Surface Properties of Epoxy Micro-N ano Composites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Epoxy micro-nano composites reinforced with silica micro filler and ion trapping nanoparticles were subjected to ultraviolet (UV) radiation for a period of 240 and 480 hours respectively. The average value of absolute space charge density increases whereas mean life time of charge decay decreases with UV ageing time. The surface potential decay characteristics of UV irradiated specimens were modelled with a double exponential function and it is noticed that the initial surface potential marginally decreases and decay rate increases with exposure to UV radiation. The increase in carrier mobility of the epoxy specimens is correlated with the increase in the density of shallow traps with UV irradiation, that occur because of the radiation induced structural degradation. The surface properties such as mean surface roughness and surface hardness tend to deteriorate after exposure to UV radiation.

articleTitle: Rice Types Classification by Using Dielectric Properties Measurement with Saline Water Increasing Technique
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of dielectric properties measurement with Saline water for classifying rice types. Open-ended coaxial probe at frequency of 20-200 MHz was applied for measuring rice properties. The rice used for this experiment included Jasmine rice 105, Hompathum rice, Chinart rice, Phitsanulok rice and Gorkor 43 rice with humidity of 8.4%, 8.2%, 8.4%, 8% and 8.4% respectively. The experiment was divided into two parts at the 25° C. The first experiment was conducted with finely ground rice. The result showed rice types cannot be classified since the dielectric properties of the rice in the experiment were very identical. The second experiment was the measurement of dialectic properties of finely ground rice mixed with saline water (water 80%: NaCI 20%) at the ratio 2:1. The results of the experiments showed that dielectric properties of rice significantly increased at low frequency. In addition, the difference could be obviously seen at the frequency of around 50 MHz, especially for the dialectic loss found in different types of rice. According to the experiment, it can be summarized that types of rice can be classified by using dielectric properties measurement along with saline water increasing techniques which can increase the dielectric instants and help blend saline water and rice well together and saline water would considerably increase dielectric loss. And then, different types of rice can be obviously identified. Consequently, both dielectric constant and dielectric loss can be used for classifying types of rice at the frequency of lower than 50 MHz. However, dielectric loss could perform better than dielectric constant for classifying types of rice.

articleTitle: Vapor-deposition polymerization and insulating characteristics of silsesquioxane thin films
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Thin films of silsesquioxane, an organic-inorganic hybrid molecule, were prepared by electron-assisted vapor deposition polymerization of its acryl monomer. It was observed that the polymerization reaction was enhanced, and the surface smoothness was improved with increasing electron current for the vapor deposition. The deposited films had dielectric breakdown strength higher than 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>V/m. Moreover, thermal stability of the insulating characteristics was improved by the electron-assisted deposition. Both dielectric constant and refractive index of the film had a tendency to decrease as the polymerization proceeds.

articleTitle: Study on Charge Distributions in Irradiated Insulation Materials of Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recent electrical insulation design under severe environment such as low air-pressure and/or high radioactive rays is required for the application to higher altitude and/or high radiation area. Under such environment, deteriorations of insulation materials due to the charge accumulation are concerned. With respect to radiation, the charging phenomena in the materials by the high energy charged particles beams, such as electrons and photons, give rise to the electric field enhancement which may cause breakdown of materials, and the power electronics equipment may become inoperable. In this paper, therefore, the experimental results of physical analyses and direct current breakdown characteristics to evaluate deterioration of the insulation materials caused by proton beam irradiation. Three results were obtained from our works. Firstly, the degree of oxidation deteriorations due to proton beam irradiations inside the insulation materials, which have some metal oxide fillers, were smaller than the material surfaces. Secondly, in the insulation materials before and after proton beam irradiations, there was no large change in the space charges and electric field distributions under applying direct current voltage. Finally, the changes of breakdown electric field strengths were generally small with proton beam irradiation current density for the above two reasons. However, the degradations such as oxidative degradations by XPS (X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy) analyses were indicated. Therefore it is necessary to evaluate the long-term breakdown characteristics in our next works.

articleTitle: Quantum Chemical Calculation Analysis of Electric Charge Trap Site in Epoxy Resin Cured Using Novel Imide Type Hardener
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Space charge accumulation characteristics in some newly developed epoxy resins at high temperature under high DC stress were investigated. While various epoxy resins are used as semiconductor packaging materials, it is expected to be improved to be available in a much severer condition under higher DC stress at higher temperatures because some semiconductor have improved to be used under such condition. For this reason, some new type epoxy resins, which are cured using some novel imide type hardeners, have been developed, and they show a high glass transition temperature. In this paper, we tried to estimate the insulating performance of them as the insulating materials at high temperatures under high electric stress. To evaluate them, the space charge accumulation characteristics in them were especially studied because the space charge accumulation is one of signs to show the materials is exposed to some situation as dangerous. As a result, it was found that the space charge accumulation is suppressed in the developed epoxy resins even at high temperatures under high DC stress. To understand the result, quantum chemical calculation analysis was also performed. Calculation results indicate that the developed epoxy resin has a deeper trap than that in the ordinary resin.

articleTitle: Contributions of Ionization and Injection to Charge Transportation in Oil-paper Insulation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Oil immersed paper is the main insulating materials used in converter transformers. Due to the structure and composition characteristics, there are many impurities in the oil immersed paper insulation and these impurities are easily ionized under the action of electric field and temperature. In previous studies, only some qualitative conclusions were given, such as the ionization charge dominates at low field strengths, while the injection charge dominates at high field strengths, but there was no in-depth study of ionized charges. In this paper, epoxy is used as a barrier material to construct a triple-layer sample (i.e. epoxy/oil immersed paper/epoxy) and a double-layer sample (i.e. epoxy/oil immersed paper). By measuring the current density of double-layer sample and triple-layer sample under different electric fields and different temperatures, the contribution of injection and ionization to charge transport in oil-paper insulation is obtained.

articleTitle: Photographic Investigation of Repetitive Pulsed Discharge Light from Needle Electrode Spraying Water
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: It is difficult to expand both streamer corona and fine droplets, simultaneously from a syringe needle. In the previous study, we succeeded in the alternate expansion of streamer corona and fine droplets from a syringe needle subjected to the rippled voltage. Electrospray was promoted when the ripple voltage had the frequency component of the natural vibration frequency of the droplet at the tip. In this study, first, the frequency of the rippled voltage was optimized. The existence probability of fine droplets tended to be high (>80<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) over a wide phase range (90-180°). Next, a nanosecond pulse was repeatedly superimposed on this rippled voltage at various phases. In the superimposition at a phase where just after the expansion, fine droplet still existed (>80%) between the electrodes, the average discharge light intensity was high. Transient discharge light was observed by using a gated image-intensifier. The streamer from a spraying needle electrode into the gas-liquid two-phase mixing-region reached the lower electrode through the spray area. This result suggests the interaction of streamer corona and fine-droplets, expanded from a syringe needle electrode.

articleTitle: Pros and Cons of THz and Far-infrared Absorption Spectroscopy Compared to Mid-infrared Absorption Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: For conducting research on dielectrics, various spectroscopic analyses must be conducted. Optical absorption spectroscopy is one of such spectroscopic measures. Fourier-transform mid-infrared (FT-MIR) absorption spectroscopy, which uses MIR photons, is very popular and it can detect intramolecular vibrations or vibrations of a relatively small chemical group that is occurring inside a molecule. In comparison, FT-far-infrared (FIR) absorption spectroscopy is suitable for the detection of vibrations of an entire molecule or those of a big chemical group. Furthermore, there is another piece of emerging absorption spectroscopy, called THz absorption spectroscopy. The THz spectroscopy is believed to be able to detect intermolecular vibrations. The pros and cons of THz and FIR absorption spectroscopy as a characterization tool for dielectric materials research are discussed.

articleTitle: Development of Pulsed Electro-acoustic Measurement System with High Positional Resolution at High Temperature using P(VDF/TrFE) Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Positional resolution of space charge distribution measurement at high temperature is attempted using a thin P(VDF/TrFE) film in PEA method. The thinnest film of a commercially available P(VDF/TrFE), which enables to detect an acoustic signal at high temperature, is about 10 μm and it is difficult to improve the positional resolution using the film. Therefore, we tried to make a thin film by ourselves by a casting method, and we can get a thin film of about 4.5 μm thick. Using the hand-made thin film, it is expected to improve the positional resolution of the space charge distribution. In this report, some typical measurement results for evaluation of the piezoelectricity in the developed film at relatively high temperature of 80 °C or more are introduced.

articleTitle: Ageing of Crepe Paper in Mineral Oil and Natural Ester
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Several billion liters of transformer oil are used in oil filled transformers worldwide. These machines are voltage transformation devices in which during their operation the heat of windings and iron core firstly is transferred to the insulation oil and then to the cooling medium. Currently, this type of transformers mainly utilizes mineral oils due to their proven good service performance. However, mineral oil has certain limitations such as their low flashpoint and biodegradability which conditions its use in indoor environments, and it may cause a high environmental impact during its use. The development of biodegradable liquids (synthetic and natural esters) has provided an alternative. Nevertheless, a question arises when natural esters are used in power transformers, are they compatible with the rest of materials used in their design. Nowadays, although several studies of accelerated thermal ageing have been undertaken there are few works that study the impact of insulation liquid and temperature on the degradation rate of other cellulosic materials such as crepe paper. This paper can take different shapes of the surface being insulated and has greater surface area which allows to retain more oil reducing the working temperature of the transformer. For this reason, this work has compared the impact of the type of insulation oil (a mineral oil and a natural ester) and the temperature (150°C, 130°C and 110°C) on lifetime of this insulation paper. Degree of polymerization has been measured to quantify the effects. Additionally, the degradation suffered by insulation oils has been evaluated through the measurement of acidity, dissipation factor and DC resistivity. It has been found that the degradation suffered by natural ester is higher than mineral oil, however, the biodegradable liquid extends the life of crepe paper.

articleTitle: Space Charge Injection Behaviors in XLPE Composite Doped with Polycyclic Aromatic Compounds Using Q(t) Method and Quantum Chemical Calculation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this study, the space charge characteristics in the polycyclic aromatic compounds doped cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) composite were analyzed by integration current (Q(t)) method and quantum chemical calculation. Experimentally, the space charge behaviors of XLPE composites modified by the three selected polycyclic aromatic compounds during polarization and depolarization process at 25 and 80 °C were measured by Q(t) method, respectively. The energy levels and 3D potential distributions of the three polycyclic aromatic compounds were calculated by density functional theory. The experimental and calculation results indicate that the polycyclic aromatic compound C with deep carrier traps and stronger polarity exhibits outstanding ability to reduce space charge injection than the others at both 25 and 80 °C. Generally, 4,4’-bis (dimethyl amino) benyil has great potential as the organic additive for DC cable insulation from the view of space charge suppression.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Emitted Frequency Spectra of Breakdowns in SF6 Gas as well as in Alternative Insulating Gases for Gas Insulated Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Due to their high current steepness, dielectric breakdowns in gaseous insulation emit electromagnetic interferences, which may disturb or even destroy electronic measuring equipment when performing breakdown tests in a laboratory. In order to analyze the emitted frequency spectra of electric breakdowns in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas as well as in alternative insulating gas mixtures, a large number of single gas breakdown tests was performed in a test vessel, and the emitted frequency spectra were measured with an antenna and a signal and spectrum analyzer. Several parameters were examined, such as gas pressure, breakdown voltage, gap distance, homogeneity and the distance between the antenna and the test vessel. With regard to the insulating gas mixture, there was no visible impact on the emitted frequency spectra. However, it could be observed that a smaller gap distance and a higher breakdown voltage, thus a higher electric field strength, lead to both higher signal amplitudes and higher maximum frequencies. Likewise, a slightly inhomogeneous electrode arrangement results in higher maximum electric field strengths and, therefore, to higher amplitudes and higher maximum frequencies than a homogeneous electrode arrangement of the same parameters.

articleTitle: Proposal of Calibration Method for Space Charge Distribution in Laminated Films Using PEA Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A calibration technique using a newly developed electrode attachment was introduced to measure space charge distribution in laminated different materials using PEA method under a high dc stress. In many cases of insulating systems, different kinds of insulating layers are used by laminating with other materials. When a DC high voltage is applied to such layers, charges usually accumulate at the interfaces between the layer and the electrode and/or in the layers. While this phenomenon was already analyzed theoretically, actual charge accumulation seems to be different from the result derived from the theoretical analysis. To understand the phenomenon, the space charge distribution has been attempted to measure in a laminated sample. To measure it correctly, a calibration method that takes into account the sound velocity and the permittivity of both the double layered sample is required. Therefore, at first, we need to get a reference signal for calibrating the correct charge distribution. In this research, we developed a measuring attachment that applied a voltage to only one of the laminated two insulating material samples to acquire the signal necessary for calibration of the double layer sample. From the results, the reference waveform of a grounded electrode side sample was calculated using the obtained reference waveform in the laminated sample, and the reference waveform of a high voltage side sample can be obtained by calculating the shared voltage applied to each sample.

articleTitle: On the Delineation of Roles of Homocharge Conduction, Injection and Diffusion in LDPE
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: With the help of experimental data in low density polyethylene (LDPE), obtained from pulsed electro-acoustic method, a significant amount of concentration gradient can be seen. However, different simulation models of homocharge accumulation present in the literature, considers only the drift phenomenon of charge carriers while neglecting the diffusion. These models envisage the homocharge formation with limited accuracy. With the help of recently published analytical equations of space charge and electric field, the individual role of conduction of charges in bulk, diffusion of charge carriers and injection from the electrodes are delineated.

articleTitle: DC Breakdown Performances of EP/TiO2 Nanocomposites at Elevated Temperatures Dominated by Carrier Traps and Molecular Chain Dynamic
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: DC breakdown is one of the underlying problems for epoxy (EP) based electrical power applications with elevated operating temperature. To investigate the breakdown mechanism at elevated temperature and improve DC breakdown strength for epoxy resin, functional nano-titania (TiO2) fillers were incorporated into epoxy matrix with four filler contents, and DC breakdown characteristics of EP/TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanocomposites were tested at four elevated temperatures, the trap characteristics were analyzed by TSC curves and a charge transport and molecular dynamic (CTMD) model was used to calculate the breakdown strength for pristine epoxy resin at elevated temperatures. It indicates that the incorporation of nano-fillers with optimal filler contents can effectively increase breakdown characteristics about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for all temperatures, DC breakdown strength owns a positive relation with the deep trap level, which proves the carrier trap is the main factor determines the breakdown strength at the same temperature. While for the breakdown at different temperature, the breakdown strength decreases with temperature exponentially. An Arrhenius formula with activation energy of 0.15 eV is used to describe the relationship between molecular chain mobility and temperature for 1 wt% EP/TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanocomposites. In this case, the simulation breakdown strengths by CTMD model exhibits greatly accordance with experimental results, which indicate the breakdown characteristics at elevated temperatures are mainly controlled by molecular chain segment dynamics. The findings in this work provide a reliable path to improve DC breakdown strength for epoxy resin at elevated temperature by tailoring carrier traps and molecular chain dynamics.

articleTitle: Dielectric Relaxation in Yttria-stabilized Zirconia Crystals
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this paper, the dielectric relaxation process in 11 mol% yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) crystals were studied by using thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC) method and the origin responsible for dielectric polarization was discussed. TSDC measurements were performed in the temperature range of 173-500 K. By fitting the measured data with theoretical TSDC curves of dipole polarization, four peaks., with the activation energy of 0.46 eV., 0.99 eV., 1.15 eV., and 2.10 eV respectively., were observed. The origin for the peaks was attributed to the different migration paths of oxygen vacancies.

articleTitle: Effect of Laminating Direction on Space Charge and Conduction Current in Laminate Elastomer Sheets
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this paper, the DC conduction current and space charge characteristics of laminate elastomer sheets with different laminating directions is investigated. Samples (N,V,H) were prepared as 3 types of the laminate elastomer sheets with different laminating directions using a stereolithographic 3D printer. Sample N has no lamination. Sample V has vertical laminating directions against sample surface. Sample H has horizontal laminating direction against sample surface. The sample thickness was around 0.5 mm and the laminating pitch was 0.05 mm. The DC conduction current was measured by using a current integration meter. Space charge distribution was measured using the pulsed electro-acoustic system. The experiments were carried out at 27 °C. The accumulated positive charge amount near the anode in sample H was found to be larger than that in V and N. The conductivity scarcely changes up to around 5 kV/mm, but rises with increase of electric field above 5 kV/mm irrespective of differences among samples.

articleTitle: Understanding the Electrical and Mechanical Properties of Epoxy Alumina Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Epoxy γ-alumina nanocomposites are prepared with different weight percentage (wt%) to understand its electrical and mechanical properties. surface potential decay rate of the material and the trap depth shows inverse correlation. Increase in dielectric constant and loss tangent is observed on addition of γ-alumina to the epoxy resin. Addition of γ-alumina nanoparticles shows reduced space charge accumulation. DMA studies indicate that the γ-alumina epoxy nanocomposites have enhanced storage modulus, glass transition temperature, and activation energy.

articleTitle: Prediction of the Space Charge Related Maximum Electric Field of XLPE Insulation by Sparse Bayesian Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Space charge dynamics and the related breakdown failure are of great importance in HVDC cable insulation. Considerable works have been studied the space charge behavior and the mechanism underlying the charge transport and accumulation inside the cable insulating materials. However, the formation, accumulation, and dissipation of space charges are still complicated, which are affected by many factors, such as electric field, temperature, voltage reversal, material morphology, etc. Actually. At present, there is still a lack of research on the relationship model of this complex nonlinear network between space charge behavior and breakdown. The maximum electric field strength is extremely important in the study of space charge characteristics and insulation breakdown, which reflects the degree of distortion of the internal electric field. This paper establishes a breakdown prediction model based on the maximum electric field. First, the PEA method is used to measure the experimental results of the space charge distribution for a long time. Then, the sparse Bayesian learning is used employed to learn the mapping relationship between the maximum field strength and the relevant parameters, and t. After that, the prediction model is established. The breakdown conditions are discussed with reference to respect to the relevant studiesprevious work. This work paper is useful to evaluate the aging and predict the insulation failure by space charge effects in HVDC cable insulation.

articleTitle: On-Line and Off-Line Partial Discharge Scouting on MV Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The evaluation of the safe and healthy operation of the electrical assets goes through the knowledge of the overall status of their conditions. In particular, the assessment of the insulation system is important, being it the root cause of most failures. Among the various measurements that can be carried out on an electrical asset, the Partial Discharge Analysis (PDA) is one of the most efficient through which the effective deterioration of the insulation systems can be assessed. Nowadays the PDA is becoming an increasingly popular practice even in the MV sector, where its spread has been encouraged not - as for in the HV - by the high cost of a single component (e.g. power transformer, high voltage cable, etc.) but by a huge number of assets and their overall aging. The asset managers through the information given by the PDA can properly operate the electrical assets and perform maintenance based on their status (Condition-Based Maintenance - CBM) instead of using an approach based on maintenance actions performed at a fixed interval of times (Time-Based Maintenance-TBM). In this paper firstly the PDA will be proposed as the basis for the CBM and then a case study about a successfully partial discharge measurement campaign on a 33kV network of an island will be presented. The data is going to be discussed are relevant to both on-line and off-line tests in which a surface/interface PD phenomenon has been detected and subsequently localized through the Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR).

articleTitle: Study on the Dielectric Performance of XLPE Nanocomposite Against The Electrical Tree Propagation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Currently, XLPE is widely used in underground high voltage cable. Recently, a few nanofillers have been selected by numerous researchers to enhance the electrical tree resistance in polymer matrix. The investigation on the electrical trees properties of unfilled XLPE and XLPE filled with ZnO, hybrid nanocomposite and Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanofillers have been carried out and described in this paper. The needle-plane electrodes were employed in this study with gap of 2mm between the electrodes. A digital camera and microscope system were used to observe the structure and growth of the electrical tree in XLPE nanocomposite. The properties of electrical trees in XLPE/ZnO, XLPE/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and hybrid nanocomposite were compared to the unfilled one. The hybrid nanconposite improve the performance of the insulator by inhibit the rapid growth of electical tree. The TIV for hybrid nanocomposite is 12.32% higher than the unfilled XLPE.

articleTitle: Effects of Thermal Aging on the Characteristics of Kraft Paper in Various Liquid Insulating Materials
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Transformer is one of the most important equipments in an electric power system. Because of thermal aging, performances of paper and oil insulations may be degraded. This paper reports experimental results on the thermal aging on kraft paper insulation in various liquid insulating materials such as mineral oil, natural ester from palm oil and gas to liquid oil under accelerated aging. Samples were conditioned to the same initial conditions through the heating at a temperature of 100 °C for 24 hours. Liquid insulation samples with volume of 200 ml and 10 gram insulating kraft paper were put in bottles with rubber seal. The paper-oil ratio reflects the typical ratio of oil and kraft paper inside a real transformer. The accelerated thermal aging was conducted in an oven with temperatures of 120°C or 150°C for up to 1008 hours. Sample were taken every two weeks (336 hours) and put into various test and measurements. For eludicating the effects of thermal aging on the kraft paper characteristics, SEM (scanning electron microscope), EDS (energy dispersive spectroscopy), DTA (differential thermal analysis) and FTIR (Fourier transform infra red) analysis were used. Degree of polymerization and tensile strength at certain aging level were also investigated. The experimental results showed that there are reduction in degree of polymerization and tensile strength of kraft paper under accelerated thermal aging. Morphological degradation in the form of microglobules in the kraft paper also can be seen from SEM (scanning electron microscope). The percentage of oxygen element reduced significantly during aging. The analysis showed that there were increase of crystallinity percentage during accelerated thermal aging compared to those of amorphous in kraft paper. FTIR analysis showed the evidence of paper oxidation to release C-O and C=O which increased by temperature and aging time.

articleTitle: The Role of Theory in Understanding Space Charge Distributions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Space charge generation in insulating polymers is a complex process involving many interlocking synergistic processes, which make the understanding of its equilibrium distributions and their evolution a very challenging problem. It is argued that the general features at equilibrium can be determined from fundamental physics, though the details depend upon many factors that are incompletely known and may even vary from sample to sample. The difference between dynamic and thermodynamic equilibrium is explored, bringing into prominence the limited timescale of laboratory experiments compared to time under service stress. The major importance of the electrode contacts of an insulating system is highlighted and it is shown that our understanding is not yet sufficient to describe injection and extraction in a simple mathematical manner. It is suggested that a way forward is to define an intermediate zone between the electrode material and bulk polymer. The effect of contact charge and carrier barriers at dielectric-dielectric interfaces is briefly touched upon, and the perils of ambiguous interpretation outlined. Finally a route map for the future is presented.

articleTitle: Comparison between Positive and Negative Corona Discharges by Hydrodynamic Plasma Simulations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Corona discharges are due to the ionization of the gas between two electrodes when the electric field near one of them is very strong. The lack of a complete understanding of the physical processes in corona discharge in both positive and negative polarity means that interest in corona discharge is still current. In this work, we use a more realistic hydrodynamic plasma model which considers 12 charged species such electron, ions and molecules, and 32 chemical reactions present in the plasma. The digital algorithm based on the finite element method is implemented using the commercial software COMSOL Multiphysics©. A geometrical configuration of a 1D-axisymmetric wire-cylinder is considered and the set of reactions takes place in the radial direction given the symmetry of the system. The results show that the electron density in the negative corona is four orders of magnitude greater than that in the positive corona. The total number of electrons in the plasma layer of the negative corona is more than 50 times that produced in the positive corona. Under identical temperature and pressure conditions, the weakest corona current in positive polarity, which implies a lower ignition DC voltage. Temperature has an opposite effect on the distribution of the electron density present in the plasma. While the rise in temperature causes a rapid increase in the density of electrons in negative corona, the increase is slower in positive corona. In both cases, the electric field is constant on the conductor surface, however the space charge modifies the local electric field.
